title.zh: 卷一百一十五 載記第十五 苻丕 苻登
title.en: Volume 115 Records 15: Fu Pi; Fu Deng
title.raw: 卷一百一十五 載記第十五 苻丕 苻登 Volume 115 Records 15: Fu Pi; Fu Deng

sentences.zh: 苻丕 苻登

translations.literal: Fu Pi; Fu Deng.
translations.idiomatic: This chapter records Fu Pi and Fu Deng.

sentences.zh: 苻丕，字永叔，堅之長庶子也。

translations.literal: Fu Pi, style name Yongshu, was Fu Jian's eldest son by a concubine.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Pi, whose courtesy name was Yongshu, was Fu Jian's eldest son born to a secondary consort.

sentences.zh: 少而聰彗好學，博綜經史。

translations.literal: From youth he was clever and fond of learning, and broadly versed in the classics and histories.
translations.idiomatic: Even as a boy he showed quick intelligence and a love of books, with wide learning in classical texts and historical works.

sentences.zh: 堅與言將略，嘉之，命鄧羌教以兵法。

translations.literal: Fu Jian discussed with him the art of generalship, praised him, and ordered Deng Qiang to instruct him in military methods.
translations.idiomatic: When Fu Jian talked strategy with him, he was so impressed that he had Deng Qiang teach the young man the arts of war.

sentences.zh: 文武才幹亞於苻融，為將善收士卒情，出鎮於鄴，東夏安之。

translations.literal: His civil and military ability was second only to Fu Rong's; as a general he was skilled at winning his soldiers' devotion. When he went out to command at Ye, the eastern regions were pacified.
translations.idiomatic: In talent for both civil and military affairs he stood just below Fu Rong, and as a commander he knew how to bind his men to him. His posting to Ye brought stability to the east.

sentences.zh: 堅敗歸長安，丕為慕容垂所逼，自鄴奔枋頭。

translations.literal: When Fu Jian was defeated and returned to Chang'an, Fu Pi was pressed by Murong Chui and fled from Ye to Fangtou.
translations.idiomatic: After Fu Jian's defeat and retreat to Chang'an, Fu Pi could not hold Ye against Murong Chui and withdrew to Fangtou.

sentences.zh: 堅之死也，丕復入鄴城，將收兵趙、魏，西赴長安。

translations.literal: When Fu Jian died, Fu Pi re-entered Ye, intending to gather troops in Zhao and Wei and march west to Chang'an.
translations.idiomatic: On Fu Jian's death, Fu Pi went back into Ye, planning to raise forces in Zhao and Wei and then strike west toward Chang'an.

sentences.zh: 會幽州刺史王永、平州刺史苻沖頻為垂將平規等所敗，乃遣昌黎太守宋敞焚燒和龍、薊城宮室，率眾三萬進屯壺關，遣使招丕。

translations.literal: It happened that the Inspector of Youzhou Wang Yong and the Inspector of Pingzhou Fu Chong were repeatedly defeated by Murong Chui's generals such as Ping Gui, so they sent the Administrator of Changli Song Chang to burn the palace buildings at Helong and Ji, led thirty thousand men to advance and encamp at Huguan, and sent envoys to summon Fu Pi.
translations.idiomatic: Meanwhile Wang Yong of Youzhou and Fu Chong of Pingzhou suffered repeated defeats at the hands of Murong Chui's officers like Ping Gui; they had Song Chang, administrator of Changli, put the palaces of Helong and Ji to the torch, moved thirty thousand troops up to Huguan, and sent messengers calling Fu Pi to join them.

sentences.zh: 丕乃去鄴，率男女六萬餘口進如潞川。

translations.literal: Fu Pi then left Ye, leading more than sixty thousand men and women to advance toward the Lu River basin.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Pi accordingly abandoned Ye and marched toward the Lu River with a train of over sixty thousand souls.

sentences.zh: 驃騎張蠔、并州刺史王騰迎之，入據晉陽，始知堅死問，舉哀于晉陽，三軍縞素。

translations.literal: The Cavalry-in-Flight general Zhang Hao and the Inspector of Bingzhou Wang Teng welcomed him; they entered and occupied Jinyang, only then learning of Fu Jian's death. They observed mourning at Jinyang, and the whole army wore white.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Hao, general of Agile Cavalry, and Wang Teng, inspector of Bingzhou, received him; together they took Jinyang, where they first heard that Fu Jian was dead. They held mourning rites there, and every soldier donned mourning white.

sentences.zh: 王永留苻沖守壺關，率騎一萬會丕，勸稱尊號，丕從之，乃乙太元十年僭即皇帝位於晉陽南。

translations.literal: Wang Yong left Fu Chong to defend Huguan, led ten thousand cavalry to join Fu Pi, urged him to assume the supreme title; Fu Pi agreed. In the tenth year of Taiyuan he unlawfully assumed the imperial dignity south of Jinyang.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Yong stationed Fu Chong at Huguan, rode out with ten thousand horse to meet Fu Pi, and pressed him to take the throne; Fu Pi consented. In the tenth year of the Taiyuan era he presumptuously declared himself emperor south of Jinyang.

sentences.zh: 立堅行廟，太赦境內，改元曰太安。

translations.literal: He established a travelling shrine to Fu Jian, granted a general amnesty within his borders, and changed the era name to Tai'an.
translations.idiomatic: He set up a mobile ancestral shrine for Fu Jian, proclaimed an amnesty throughout his territory, and adopted the reign title Tai'an.

sentences.zh: 置百官，以張蠔為侍中、司空，封上黨郡公；

translations.literal: He appointed the full official roster, making Zhang Hao Palace Attendant and Minister of Works, enfeoffing him as Duke of Shangdang commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Among his appointments, Zhang Hao became palace attendant and minister of works, with the ducal title of Shangdang.

sentences.zh: 王永為使持節、侍中、都督中外諸軍事、車騎大將軍、尚書令，進封清河公；

translations.literal: Wang Yong was made Bearer of the Imperial Insignia, Palace Attendant, Commander-in-Chief of All Military Affairs Within and Without, General of Chariots and Cavalry, Director of the Secretariat, and advanced to Duke of Qinghe.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Yong received the titles bearer of the imperial tally, palace attendant, commander of all armies at court and in the field, general of chariots and cavalry, and director of the secretariat, and was promoted to duke of Qinghe.

sentences.zh: 王騰為散騎常侍、中軍大將軍、司隸校尉、陽平郡公；

translations.literal: Wang Teng was made Cavalier Attendant-in-Ordinary, General of the Central Army, Colonel Director of Retainers, and Duke of Yangping commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Teng was named cavalier attendant-in-ordinary, general of the central army, colonel director of retainers, and duke of Yangping.

sentences.zh: 苻沖為左光祿大夫、尚書左僕射、西平王；

translations.literal: Fu Chong was made Grand Master of the Left, Vice Director of the Left of the Secretariat, and Prince of Xiping.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Chong became grand master of the left, left vice director of the secretariat, and prince of Xiping.

sentences.zh: 俱石子為衛將軍、濮陽公；

translations.literal: Ju Shizi was made General of the Guards and Duke of Puyang.
translations.idiomatic: Ju Shizi was appointed general of the guards and duke of Puyang.

sentences.zh: 楊輔為尚書右僕射、濟陽公；

translations.literal: Yang Fu was made Vice Director of the Right of the Secretariat and Duke of Jiyang.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Fu took the posts of right vice director of the secretariat and duke of Jiyang.

sentences.zh: 王亮為護軍將軍、彭城公；

translations.literal: Wang Liang was made General Who Protects the Army and Duke of Pengcheng.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Liang became general who guards the army and duke of Pengcheng.

sentences.zh: 強益耳、梁暢為侍中，徐義為吏部尚書，並封縣公。

translations.literal: Qiang Yier and Liang Chang were made Palace Attendants, Xu Yi Director of the Ministry of Personnel, and all were enfeoffed as Dukes of counties.
translations.idiomatic: Qiang Yier and Liang Chang were named palace attendants, Xu Yi director of personnel, and each received a county ducal fief.

sentences.zh: 自余封授各有差。

translations.literal: The remaining appointments and enfeoffments each had their gradations.
translations.idiomatic: Other offices and noble ranks were distributed according to merit and station.

sentences.zh: 是時安西呂光自西域還師，至於宜禾，堅涼州刺史梁熙謀閉境距之。

translations.literal: At this time the General Who Pacifies the West Lü Guang was returning his army from the Western Regions and reached Yihe; Liang Xi, Fu Jian's Inspector of Liangzhou, planned to close the border and keep him out.
translations.idiomatic: Meanwhile Lü Guang, general who pacifies the west, was marching home from the Western Regions and had reached Yihe; Liang Xi, inspector of Liangzhou under Fu Jian, meant to shut the frontier and block his entry.

sentences.zh: 高昌太守楊翰言於熙曰：「「呂光新定西國，兵強氣銳，其鋒不可當也。

translations.literal: The Administrator of Gaochang Yang Han spoke to Xi, saying: "Lü Guang has newly subdued the western lands; his troops are strong and his morale keen, and the edge of his advance cannot be withstood.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Han, administrator of Gaochang, warned Liang Xi: "Lü Guang has just brought the west under his hand; his soldiers are fresh and fierce, and nothing can stand in the path of his thrust.

sentences.zh: 度其事意，必有異圖。

translations.literal: Considering the drift of events, he is sure to harbor other designs.
translations.idiomatic: Judging from how things are moving, he must be nursing ambitions beyond a simple homecoming.

sentences.zh: 且今關中擾亂，京師存亡未知，自河已西迄於流沙，地方萬里，帶甲十萬，鼎峙之勢實在今日。

translations.literal: Moreover the Guanzhong is in turmoil, and whether the capital survives is unknown; from the Yellow River westward to the shifting sands, the territory is ten thousand li, with a hundred thousand armored men—the time for a tripartite standoff is truly now.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover Guanzhong is chaos and the fate of the capital uncertain; west of the Yellow River stretches ten thousand li of ground to the desert's edge, garrisoned by a hundred thousand men—if ever there was a moment for contending powers to face one another, it is this.

sentences.zh: 若光出流沙，其勢難測。

translations.literal: If Lü Guang emerges from the desert, his movements will be hard to predict.
translations.idiomatic: Once Lü Guang breaks out of the western wastes, no one can tell what he will do next.

sentences.zh: 高梧穀口，水險之要，宜先守之而奪其水。

translations.literal: Gaowu Gorge is a choke point of water and terrain; you should seize it first and cut off his water supply.
translations.idiomatic: Gaowu Gorge is a defile where water and ground favor the defender; hold it first and deny him water.

sentences.zh: 彼既窮渴，自然投戈。

translations.literal: When they are exhausted and parched, they will naturally cast aside their weapons.
translations.idiomatic: Thirst and exhaustion will do your work for you—they will throw down their arms of their own accord.

sentences.zh: 如其以遠不守，伊吾之關亦可距也。

translations.literal: If he disdains to hold that distant line, the pass at Yiwu can still bar him.
translations.idiomatic: Even if he scorns to contest that distant ground, the Yiwu barrier can still block him.

sentences.zh: 若度此二要，雖有子房之策，難為計矣。

translations.literal: If he passes these two critical points, even with a Zhang Liang's stratagems you will find no remedy.
translations.idiomatic: Let him through both choke points, and not even Zhang Liang's cunning could save your position.

sentences.zh: 地有所必爭，真此機也。

translations.literal: There are positions that must be fought for—this is the moment.
translations.idiomatic: Some ground must be contested at any cost; the opportunity is now.

sentences.zh: 」熙弗從。

translations.literal: " Xi did not follow this advice.
translations.idiomatic: " Liang Xi refused to listen.

sentences.zh: 美水令犍為張統說熙曰：「主上傾國南討，覆敗而還。

translations.literal: The magistrate of Meishui, Zhang Tong of Qianwei, urged Xi, saying: "The sovereign raised the whole realm for a southern expedition and came back in ruin.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Tong of Qianwei, magistrate of Meishui, said to Liang Xi: "Our lord emptied the kingdom for a southern campaign and returned in defeat.

sentences.zh: 慕容垂擅兵河北，泓、沖寇逼京師，丁零雜虜，跋扈關、洛，州郡奸豪，所在風扇，王綱弛絕，人懷利己。

translations.literal: Murong Chui wields arms north of the Yellow River; Hong and Chong press the capital; Dingling and mixed barbarians run riot in Guan and Luo; unscrupulous strongmen in every province rise like windblown grass; the royal net hangs slack and each man seeks his private gain.
translations.idiomatic: Murong Chui holds the Hebei plain; Murong Hong and Murong Chong threaten the capital; Dingling and other tribes rampage through Guanzhong and the Luoyang region; local magnates everywhere take the cue to rebel; imperial authority frays and every hand reaches for advantage.

sentences.zh: 今呂光回師，將軍何以抗也？

translations.literal: Now Lü Guang is leading his army back—how will you, General, resist him?
translations.idiomatic: Lü Guang is marching home at the head of a seasoned host—how do you mean to stop him?

sentences.zh: 」熙曰：「誠深憂之，未知計之所出。

translations.literal: " Xi said: "I am deeply troubled, but I do not know what plan to adopt.
translations.idiomatic: " Liang Xi answered, "The danger weighs on me, yet I see no clear course.

sentences.zh: 」統曰：「光雄果勇毅，明略絕人，今以蕩西域之威，擁歸師之銳，鋒若猛火之盛于原，弗可敵也。

translations.literal: " Tong said: "Lü Guang is bold, resolute, and brave beyond ordinary men; now, with the prestige of having swept the Western Regions and the keen edge of a homecoming army, his spearhead is like a fierce fire racing across the plain—he cannot be opposed.
translations.idiomatic: " Zhang Tong replied, "Lü Guang is a fighter of rare courage and cunning; fresh from conquering the west and leading veterans homeward, he strikes like wildfire across dry grass—you cannot meet him head-on.

sentences.zh: 將軍世受殊恩，忠誠夙著，立勳王室，宜在於今。

translations.literal: The General's house has received singular favor for generations, your loyalty has long been manifest, and you have raised achievements for the royal house—this is the moment to show it.
translations.idiomatic: Your family has enjoyed extraordinary grace, your devotion has never been in doubt, and you have served the throne with distinction—now is the hour to prove it again.

sentences.zh: 行唐公洛，上之從弟，勇冠一時。

translations.literal: The Duke of Xingtang, Luo, is His Majesty's younger cousin by the same grandfather; his valor is unmatched in the age.
translations.idiomatic: The duke of Xingtang, Fu Luo, is the emperor's cousin on the father's side and the foremost warrior of his day.

sentences.zh: 為將軍計者，莫若奉為盟主，以攝眾望，推忠義以總率群豪，則光無異心也。

translations.literal: For the General's planning, nothing would be better than to acknowledge him as covenant lord to gather popular expectation, and to rally the bold with loyalty and righteousness—then Lü Guang will have no separate ambition.
translations.idiomatic: The wise course is to recognize Fu Luo as leader of the alliance and win the people's hope, then gather the heroes under the banner of duty—so Lü Guang finds no opening for disloyalty.

sentences.zh: 資其精銳，東兼毛興，連王統、楊璧，集四州之眾，掃凶逆于諸夏，甯帝室於關中，此桓文之舉也。

translations.literal: With his picked troops strike east to absorb Mao Xing, join Wang Tong and Yang Bi, assemble the hosts of four provinces, sweep the rebels from the central plains, and restore the imperial house in Guanzhong—this is the deed of a Huan or a Wen.
translations.idiomatic: Use his elite columns to drive east, link with Mao Xing, Wang Tong, and Yang Bi, combine the armies of four provinces, clear the heartland of traitors, and set the dynasty right in Guanzhong—work worthy of Duke Huan or Duke Wen.

sentences.zh: 」熙又不從。

translations.literal: " Again Xi did not follow.
translations.idiomatic: " Liang Xi still would not take the advice.

sentences.zh: 殺洛於西海，以子胤為鷹揚將軍，率眾五萬距光於酒泉。

translations.literal: He killed Luo at Xihai, appointed his son Yin General Who Spreads Might, and led fifty thousand men to oppose Lü Guang at Jiuquan.
translations.idiomatic: Instead he executed Fu Luo at Xihai, named his son Yin general who spreads might, and sent fifty thousand soldiers to block Lü Guang at Jiuquan.

sentences.zh: 敦煌太守姚靜、晉昌太守李純以郡降光。

translations.literal: The Administrator of Dunhuang Yao Jing and the Administrator of Jinchang Li Chun surrendered their commanderies to Lü Guang.
translations.idiomatic: Yao Jing of Dunhuang and Li Chun of Jinchang yielded their prefectures to Lü Guang.

sentences.zh: 胤及光戰于安彌，為光所敗。

translations.literal: Yin fought Lü Guang at Anmi and was defeated by him.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Yin met Lü Guang at Anmi and was routed.

sentences.zh: 武威太守彭濟執熙迎光，光殺之。

translations.literal: The Administrator of Wuwei Peng Ji seized Xi and welcomed Lü Guang; Lü Guang killed Xi.
translations.idiomatic: Peng Ji, administrator of Wuwei, took Liang Xi prisoner and opened the gates to Lü Guang, who then put Liang Xi to death.

sentences.zh: 建威、西郡太守索泮，奮威、督洪池已南諸軍事、酒泉太守宋皓等，並為光所殺。

translations.literal: Suo Pan, administrator of Jianwei and Xijun, and Song Hao, administrator of Jiuquan who held the office of general who rouses might and supervised military affairs south of Hongchi Pool, together with others, were all killed by Lü Guang.
translations.idiomatic: Suo Pan, who held Jianwei and the western commandery, Song Hao of Jiuquan—who served as general who rouses might and directed troops south of Hongchi—and others likewise fell to Lü Guang's blade.

sentences.zh: 堅尚書令、魏昌公苻纂自關中來奔，拜太尉，進封東海王。

translations.literal: Fu Jian's Director of the Secretariat and Duke of Weichang Fu Zuan came fleeing from Guanzhong and was appointed Grand Commandant, advanced to Prince of Donghai.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Zuan, Fu Jian's director of the secretariat and duke of Weichang, arrived as a refugee from Guanzhong; Fu Pi named him grand commandant and raised him to prince of Donghai.

sentences.zh: 以中山太守王兗為平東將軍、平州刺史、阜城侯，苻定為征東將軍、冀州牧、高城侯，苻紹為鎮東將軍、督冀州諸軍事、重合侯，苻謨為征西將軍、幽州牧、高邑侯，苻亮為鎮北大將軍、督幽、并二州諸軍事，並進爵郡公。

translations.literal: He made the Administrator of Zhongshan Wang Yan General Who Pacifies the East, Inspector of Pingzhou, and Marquis of Fucheng; Fu Ding General Who Conquers the East, Governor of Jizhou, and Marquis of Gaocheng; Fu Shao General Who Guards the East, Supervisor of Military Affairs in Jizhou, and Marquis of Chonghe; Fu Mo General Who Conquers the West, Governor of Youzhou, and Marquis of Gaoyi; Fu Liang General Who Guards the North, Commander of Military Affairs in You and Bing, and all were advanced in noble rank to Dukes of commanderies.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Yan of Zhongshan became general who pacifies the east, inspector of Pingzhou, and marquis of Fucheng; Fu Ding general who conquers the east, governor of Jizhou, and marquis of Gaocheng; Fu Shao general who guards the east, with overall command in Jizhou, and marquis of Chonghe; Fu Mo general who conquers the west, governor of Youzhou, and marquis of Gaoyi; Fu Liang general who guards the north, with joint authority over You and Bing—all were promoted to commandery dukes.

sentences.zh: 定、紹據信都，謨、亮先據常山，慕容垂之圍鄴城也，並降于垂，聞丕稱尊號，遣使謝罪。

translations.literal: Ding and Shao held Xindu; Mo and Liang had first occupied Changshan; when Murong Chui besieged Ye they had both surrendered to Chui, but on hearing that Fu Pi had assumed the imperial title they sent envoys to apologize.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Ding and Fu Shao held Xindu while Fu Mo and Fu Liang had seized Changshan first; both pairs had gone over to Murong Chui when he invested Ye, yet when Fu Pi declared himself emperor they dispatched messengers begging forgiveness.

sentences.zh: 王兗固守博陵，與垂相持。

translations.literal: Wang Yan stubbornly defended Boling against Chui.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Yan shut himself in Boling and held the line against Murong Chui.

sentences.zh: 左將軍竇沖、秦州刺史王統、河州刺史毛興、益州刺史王廣、南秦州刺史楊璧、衛將軍楊定，並據隴右，遣使招丕，請討姚萇。

translations.literal: The General of the Left Dou Chong, the Inspector of Qinzhou Wang Tong, the Inspector of Hezhou Mao Xing, the Inspector of Yizhou Wang Guang, the Inspector of South Qinzhou Yang Bi, and the General of the Guards Yang Ding all held Longyou and sent envoys to summon Fu Pi, asking to campaign against Yao Chang.
translations.idiomatic: Dou Chong, general of the left; Wang Tong, inspector of Qinzhou; Mao Xing, inspector of Hezhou; Wang Guang, inspector of Yizhou; Yang Bi, inspector of south Qinzhou; and Yang Ding, general of the guards, each held ground in Longyou and wrote to Fu Pi offering to strike Yao Chang.

sentences.zh: 丕大悅，以定為驃騎大將軍、雍州牧，沖為征西大將軍、梁州牧，統鎮西大將軍，興車騎大將軍，璧征南大將軍，並開府儀同三司，加散騎常侍，廣安西將軍，皆進位州牧。

translations.literal: Fu Pi was greatly pleased; he made Yang Ding Grand General of Agile Cavalry and Governor of Yongzhou, Chong Grand General Who Conquers the West and Governor of Liangzhou, Tong Grand General Who Guards the West, Xing Grand General of Chariots and Cavalry, Bi Grand General Who Conquers the South, all with the privilege of opening a general's office with ceremony equal to the Three Excellencies and the additional title of Cavalier Attendant-in-Ordinary, Guang General Who Pacifies the West, all advanced to the position of provincial governor.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Pi was delighted: Yang Ding became grand general of agile cavalry and governor of Yongzhou; Dou Chong grand general who conquers the west and governor of Liangzhou; Wang Tong grand general who guards the west; Mao Xing grand general of chariots and cavalry; Yang Bi grand general who conquers the south—each with an independent headquarters and honors matching the three dukes, plus the title cavalier attendant-in-ordinary; Wang Guang became general who pacifies the west; all were raised to governorships.

sentences.zh: 於是王永宣檄州郡曰：「大行皇帝棄背萬國，四海無主。

translations.literal: Thereupon Wang Yong proclaimed to the provinces and commanderies: "The late emperor has left the myriad states; within the four seas there is no lord.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Yong then circulated a manifesto: "The great emperor has departed this life, and the realm has no sovereign.

sentences.zh: 征東大將軍、長樂公，先帝元子，聖武自天，受命荊南，威振衡海，分陝東都，道被夷夏，仁澤光於宇宙，德聽侔于《下武》。

translations.literal: The General Who Conquers the East, Duke of Changle, the late emperor's eldest son by the principal consort, is sacred and martial as Heaven itself; he received his mandate south of the Jing, his might shook Heng and the sea; he divided the burden east of the Mount, his way spread through barbarian and Chinese alike; his kindly grace shone through the cosmos, and his virtuous fame matches the ode 'Lower Martial.'
translations.idiomatic: The general who conquers the east and duke of Changle—firstborn of the late sovereign—is heaven-endowed in arms and majesty; invested on the southern Jing, his terror reached the Xiang basin and the coast; charged with the eastern heartland, his influence touched both Yi and Xia; his benevolence fills heaven and earth, and his name belongs beside the kings praised in the Shijing's 'Lower Martial.'

sentences.zh: 永與司空蠔等謹順天人之望，以季秋吉辰奉公紹承大統，銜哀即事，棲穀總戎，枕戈待旦，志雪大恥。

translations.literal: Yong and Minister Zhang Hao and others respectfully followed the expectation of Heaven and men; on an auspicious day in late autumn they supported the Duke to inherit the great succession; bearing grief they took up affairs, dwelt in hardship and commanded the hosts, slept on their spears and awaited dawn, resolved to wash away the great shame.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Yong, Minister Zhang Hao, and their colleagues bowed to the will of heaven and the people; on a propitious autumn day they raised the duke to the throne. In mourning they took the reins, enduring want while they led the armies, every night with weapons at hand, burning to avenge the national humiliation.

sentences.zh: 慕容垂為封豕於關東，泓、沖繼凶於京邑，致乘輿播越，宗社淪傾。

translations.literal: Murong Chui is a great boar east of the pass; Hong and Chong continued the villainy at the capital, causing the imperial carriage to be driven afar and the altars of state to topple.
translations.idiomatic: Murong Chui is a ravening beast in the lands east of Hangu; Murong Hong and Murong Chong carried on their crimes at the capital until the emperor was forced to flee and the dynasty's foundations cracked.

sentences.zh: 羌賊姚萇，我之牧士，乘釁滔天，親行大逆，有生之巨賊也。

translations.literal: The Qiang bandit Yao Chang, once our herdsman, exploited the breach to outrage heaven, himself committing the great treason—he is the greatest villain among the living.
translations.idiomatic: The Qiang renegade Yao Chang, whom we once trusted as a provincial shepherd, seized the chaos to rebel against heaven and with his own hands wrought regicide—there is no greater traitor under the sun.

sentences.zh: 永累葉受恩，世荷將相，不與驪山之戎、滎澤之狄共戴皇天，同履厚土。

translations.literal: Yong's family for generations received favor and for ages bore ministerial and general's rank; we do not together with the Rong of Lishan or the Di of Xingze wear the bright sky and tread the thick earth.
translations.idiomatic: My house has drunk deep of imperial grace and long worn the seals of chancellor and commander; I will not stand under the same sky or walk the same soil as the Rong of Mount Li or the Di of Xingze.

sentences.zh: 諸牧伯公侯或宛沛宗臣，或四七勳舊，豈忍舍破國之醜豎，縱殺君之逆賊乎！

translations.literal: You shepherds, dukes, and marquises—some are old kin of the house of Wan and Pei, some are meritorious servants from the founding age—how can you bear to cling to a wretch who has shattered the state and indulge a regicide!
translations.idiomatic: Governors and nobles—whether ancient vassals of the blood or veterans of the rise of Qin—can you truly stomach serving the brute who broke the kingdom and the murderer who slew your king?

sentences.zh: 主上飛龍九五，實協天心，靈祥休瑞，史不輟書，投戈效義之士三十餘萬，少康、光武之功可旬朔而成。

translations.literal: The sovereign has mounted the throne as the dragon among men; it truly accords with heaven's mind; auspicious signs and felicitous omens fill the histories without pause; men who cast aside arms and came over in righteousness number more than three hundred thousand—the achievements of Shaokang or Guangwu can be completed in a matter of weeks.
translations.idiomatic: Our lord sits as the true Son of Heaven, in perfect harmony with heaven's intent; good omens crowd the annals; three hundred thousand warriors have already laid down old loyalties to join the rightful cause—the restoration of Shaokang or Guangwu can be finished in a single turning of the month.

sentences.zh: 今以衛將軍俱石子為前軍師，司空張蠔為中軍都督。

translations.literal: Now the General of the Guards Ju Shizi is made Forward Army Director; Minister Zhang Hao is Commander of the Central Army.
translations.idiomatic: Ju Shizi, general of the guards, is appointed director of the vanguard; Minister Zhang Hao commands the center.

sentences.zh: 武將猛士，風烈雷震，志殄元凶，義無他顧。

translations.literal: The fierce generals and stalwart soldiers are like wind and thunder in their fury; their will is to exterminate the arch-criminal; in righteousness they look to nothing else.
translations.idiomatic: Our champions march like storm and lightning; their sole aim is to destroy the chief enemy, and duty allows no other thought.

sentences.zh: 永謹奉乘輿，恭行天罰。

translations.literal: Yong respectfully upholds the imperial carriage and reverently executes heaven's punishment.
translations.idiomatic: I, Wang Yong, will escort the throne and carry out the sentence heaven has passed on the traitors.

sentences.zh: 君臣終始之義，在三忘軀之誠，戮力同之，以建晉、鄭之美。」

translations.literal: The righteousness that binds lord and minister from first to last, and the loyalty that in the three bonds forgets one's body—let us join our strength in this and build a merit like that of Jin and Zheng."
translations.idiomatic: Between sovereign and servant there is a bond that runs from beginning to end; in the three great relationships a loyal man gives his life without hesitation—let us strive together and leave a story worthy of the dukes of Jin and Zheng."

sentences.zh: 先是，慕容驎攻王兗於博陵，至是糧竭矢盡，郡功曹張猗逾城聚眾應驎。

translations.literal: Earlier, Murong Lin had attacked Wang Yan at Boling; by now grain and arrows were exhausted, and the county merit officer Zhang Yi climbed the wall, gathered a crowd, and went over to Lin.
translations.idiomatic: Before this, Murong Lin had been besieging Wang Yan in Boling; supplies and arrows ran out, and Zhang Yi, the county merit clerk, scaled the walls, raised a band of followers, and opened the city to Lin.

sentences.zh: 袞臨城數之曰：「卿，秦之人也。

translations.literal: Yan stood on the wall and rebuked him, saying: "You are a man of Qin.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Yan appeared on the battlements and cried out, "You were born a subject of Qin.

sentences.zh: 吾，卿之君也。

translations.literal: I am your lord.
translations.idiomatic: I am the lord you serve.

sentences.zh: 起眾應賊，號稱義兵，何名實相違之甚！

translations.literal: You raised a host to answer the bandit and call it a righteous army—how far name and fact are twisted!
translations.idiomatic: You rouse the people for the rebels yet name it a loyal host—never was deed and title so at odds!

sentences.zh: 卿兄往合鄉宗，親逐城主，天地不容，為世大戮。

translations.literal: Your elder brother once joined your village kin, personally drove out the city's master; heaven and earth would not shelter him—he became the great criminal of his age.
translations.idiomatic: Your brother once mustered the clan, chased the lawful governor from the walls, and earned the scorn of heaven and earth—a public enemy while he lived.

sentences.zh: 身滅未幾，卿復續之。

translations.literal: His person was destroyed not long ago, and you have taken up his course.
translations.idiomatic: He has scarcely paid for his crimes in the grave, and you follow in his footsteps.

sentences.zh: 卿見為吾吏，親尋干戈，競為戎首，為爾君者，不亦難乎！

translations.literal: You have been my officer, yet you personally took up arms and strove to be chief among the barbarians—for your lord, is that not hard indeed!
translations.idiomatic: You served under my banner, then seized weapons with your own hands and led the alien host—what lord could forgive such a thing?

sentences.zh: 今人何取卿一切之功，寧能忘卿不忠不孝之事！

translations.literal: What do men value in your petty moment of glory—can they forget your deeds of disloyalty and unfilial impiety!
translations.idiomatic: Men may praise your little coup today, but they will not forget that you are faithless to your prince and heartless toward your kin!

sentences.zh: 古人有雲，求忠臣必出孝子之門，卿母在城，不能顧之，何忠義之可望！

translations.literal: The ancients said, seek loyal ministers among the households of filial sons; your mother is inside the city and you do not care for her—what loyalty or righteousness can be expected!
translations.idiomatic: The old proverb runs that loyal servants come from filial homes; your mother is trapped in this town while you betray it—where is your duty or your honor?

sentences.zh: 惡不絕世，卿之謂也。

translations.literal: Evil does not die with the generation—this is said of you.
translations.idiomatic: They say wickedness outlives a single life—you prove the saying.

sentences.zh: 不圖中州禮義之邦邦，而卿門風若斯。

translations.literal: I did not expect that in the Central Plains, the land of ritual and propriety, the conduct of your clan should be thus.
translations.idiomatic: I never thought to see, in the heartland where rites and duty are taught, a family sink to such conduct as yours.

sentences.zh: 卿去老母如脫屣，吾復何論哉！

translations.literal: You cast off your aged mother as one casts off worn shoes—what more is there for me to say!
translations.idiomatic: You abandoned your old mother like a pair of worn-out sandals—I have nothing left to say to you!

sentences.zh: 」既而城陷，兗及固安侯苻鑒，並為驎所殺。

translations.literal: " Soon the city fell; Yan and the Marquis of Gu'an Fu Jian were both killed by Lin.
translations.idiomatic: " The city soon fell; Wang Yan and Fu Jian, marquis of Gu'an, were both slain by Murong Lin.

sentences.zh: 丕復以王永為司徒、錄尚書事，徐義為尚書令，加右光祿大夫。

translations.literal: Fu Pi again made Wang Yong Minister of Education and Recorder of Secretariat Affairs, Xu Yi Director of the Secretariat, with the additional title Grand Master of the Right.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Pi reappointed Wang Yong minister of education and chief of the secretariat, and Xu Yi director of the secretariat with the added honor grand master of the right.

sentences.zh: 初，王廣還自成都也，奔其兄秦州刺史統。

translations.literal: Earlier, when Wang Guang returned from Chengdu, he fled to his elder brother the Inspector of Qinzhou Wang Tong.
translations.idiomatic: When Wang Guang withdrew from Chengdu, he had thrown in with his brother Wang Tong, inspector of Qinzhou.

sentences.zh: 及長安不守，廣攻河州牧毛興於枹罕。

translations.literal: When Chang'an was lost, Guang attacked the Governor of Hezhou Mao Xing at Fuhan.
translations.idiomatic: After Chang'an fell, Wang Guang laid siege to Mao Xing, governor of Hezhou, in Fuhan.

sentences.zh: 興遣建節將軍、臨清柏衛平率其宗人千七百夜擊廣軍，大敗之。

translations.literal: Xing sent the General Who Establishes the Lineage, Bai Wei of Linqing, leading seventeen hundred of his clansmen by night to strike Guang's army and inflicted a great defeat on them.
translations.idiomatic: Mao Xing dispatched Bai Wei of Linqing, general who establishes the lineage, with seventeen hundred kinsmen in a night attack that shattered Wang Guang's camp.

sentences.zh: 王統復遣兵助廣，興於是嬰城固守。

translations.literal: Wang Tong again sent troops to aid Guang, whereupon Xing closed the city and defended it stubbornly.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Tong sent reinforcements for his brother; Mao Xing then barred the gates and held out.

sentences.zh: 既而襲王廣，敗之，廣亡奔秦州，為隴西鮮卑匹蘭所執，送詣姚萇。

translations.literal: Later he raided Wang Guang, defeated him, and Guang fled to Qinzhou, where he was seized by the Xianbei of Longxi Pilan and delivered to Yao Chang.
translations.idiomatic: He then sortied against Wang Guang, broke him, and drove him to Qinzhou, where Longxi Xianbei under Pilan took him prisoner and sent him to Yao Chang.

sentences.zh: 興既敗王廣，謀伐王統，平上邽。

translations.literal: After Xing had defeated Wang Guang, he planned to attack Wang Tong and take Shanggui.
translations.idiomatic: Once Mao Xing had beaten Wang Guang, he turned toward Wang Tong and meant to seize Shanggui.

sentences.zh: 袍罕諸氐皆窘於兵革而疲不堪命，乃殺興，推衛平為使持節、安西將軍、河州刺史，遣使請命。

translations.literal: The Di of Fuhan were all harried by war and too worn to obey; they killed Xing, raised Wei Ping to Bearer of the Imperial Insignia, General Who Pacifies the West, and Inspector of Hezhou, and sent envoys to ask for orders.
translations.idiomatic: The Di clans of Fuhan, battered by constant fighting, could bear no more; they assassinated Mao Xing, proclaimed Wei Ping inspector of Hezhou with the titles bearer of the imperial tally and general who pacifies the west, and begged the court for confirmation.

sentences.zh: 刁雲殺慕容忠，乃推慕容永為使持節、大都督中外諸軍事、大將軍、大單于、雍、秦、梁、涼四州牧、錄尚書事、河東王、稱籓於垂。

translations.literal: Diao Yun killed Murong Zhong; thereupon he raised Murong Yong to Bearer of the Imperial Insignia, Commander-in-Chief of All Military Affairs Within and Without, Grand General, Grand Chanyu, Governor of Yong, Qin, Liang, and Liang (four provinces), Recorder of Secretariat Affairs, Prince of Hedong, and he declared himself Murong Chui's vassal.
translations.idiomatic: Diao Yun slew Murong Zhong and then installed Murong Yong as commander of all armies, grand general, great chanyu, governor of four provinces, chief of the secretariat, and prince of Hedong, while acknowledging Murong Chui as overlord.

sentences.zh: 征東苻定、鎮東苻紹、征北苻謨、鎮北苻亮皆降于慕容垂。

translations.literal: The General Who Conquers the East Fu Ding, the General Who Guards the East Fu Shao, the General Who Conquers the North Fu Mo, and the General Who Guards the North Fu Liang all surrendered to Murong Chui.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Ding, Fu Shao, Fu Mo, and Fu Liang—generals of the east and north—each capitulated to Murong Chui.

sentences.zh: 丕又進王永為左丞相，苻纂為大司馬，張蠔為太尉，王騰為驃騎大將軍、儀同三司，徐義為司空，苻沖為車騎大將軍、尚書令、儀同三司，俱石子為衛大將軍、尚書左僕射，領官皆如故。

translations.literal: Fu Pi further advanced Wang Yong to Left Chancellor, Fu Zuan to Grand Marshal, Zhang Hao to Grand Commandant, Wang Teng to Grand General of Agile Cavalry with ceremony equal to the Three Excellencies, Xu Yi to Minister of Works, Fu Chong to Grand General of Chariots and Cavalry, Director of the Secretariat, with ceremony equal to the Three Excellencies, Ju Shizi to Grand General of the Guards, Left Vice Director of the Secretariat; their other posts remained as before.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Pi promoted Wang Yong to left chancellor, Fu Zuan to grand marshal, Zhang Hao to grand commandant, Wang Teng to grand general of agile cavalry with three-excellency honors, Xu Yi to minister of works, Fu Chong to grand general of chariots and cavalry and director of the secretariat with three-excellency rank, Ju Shizi to grand general of the guards and left vice director of the secretariat, leaving their remaining titles unchanged.

sentences.zh: 永又檄州郡曰：「昔夏有窮夷之難，少康起焉；

translations.literal: Yong again circulated a summons to the provinces: "Of old, when the Xia faced the calamity of Youqiong Yi, Shaokang arose;
translations.idiomatic: Wang Yong issued another call: "When the Xia faced the rebellion of Youqiong Yi, Shaokang restored the house;

sentences.zh: 王莽毒殺平帝，世祖重光漢道；

translations.literal: Wang Mang poisoned the Emperor Ping, and the Founding Emperor renewed the light of Han;
translations.idiomatic: Wang Mang murdered Emperor Ping, and Guangwu relit the Han flame;

sentences.zh: 百六之運，何代無之！

translations.literal: the cycle of the hundred and six—what age has lacked it!
translations.idiomatic: the turn of fate that brings ruin and renewal—no generation escapes it.

sentences.zh: 天降喪亂，羌胡猾夏，先帝晏駕賊庭，京師鞠為戎穴，神州蕭條，生靈塗炭。

translations.literal: Heaven sends down mourning and chaos; Qiang and Hu ravage the Hua lands; the late emperor ended his days in the bandit court; the capital has become a den of barbarians; the divine land withers and living souls are smeared with blood.
translations.idiomatic: Heaven afflicts us with mourning and rebellion; northern tribes trample the central plains; our late sovereign died in captivity; the capital is a lair of aliens; the heartland lies desolate and the people are ground to dust.

sentences.zh: 天未亡秦，社稷有奉。

translations.literal: Heaven has not yet destroyed Qin; the altars still have their keeper.
translations.idiomatic: Yet heaven has not annulled the mandate of Qin; the dynasty still has one to hold the sacrifice.

sentences.zh: 主上聖德恢弘，道侔光武，所在宅心，天人歸屬，必當隆中興之功，復配天之美。

translations.literal: The sovereign's sacred virtue is vast, his way matches Guangwu; wherever he dwells, hearts turn to him; heaven and men attach themselves; he is sure to achieve the work of a middle restoration and again match the beauty of heaven's partner.
translations.idiomatic: Our lord's virtue is boundless as Guangwu's; every land where his banner appears rallies to him; heaven and humanity are on his side—the middle revival is certain, and he will once more stand as heaven's true consort on earth.

sentences.zh: 姚萇殘虐，慕容垂凶暴，所過滅戶夷煙，毀發丘墓，毒遍存亡，痛纏幽顯，雖黃巾之害於九州，赤眉之暴于四海，方之未為甚也。

translations.literal: Yao Chang is cruel and violent, Murong Chui fierce and tyrannical; wherever they pass they wipe out households and smoke out the living, dig up tombs of dead and living alike; their poison reaches both worlds, and grief binds the manifest and hidden—though the Yellow Turbans harmed the nine provinces and the Red Eyebrows terrorized the four seas, compared with these two they were not so extreme.
translations.idiomatic: Yao Chang delights in cruelty, Murong Chui in savagery; their armies erase whole communities, strip the land to ash, and rifle graves so that neither the quick nor the dead know peace; if the Yellow Turbans scourged the realm and the Red Eyebrows looted every quarter, these two still outdo them in wickedness.

sentences.zh: 今素秋將及，行師令辰，公侯牧守，壘主鄉豪，或戮力國家，乃心王室，各率所統，以孟冬上旬會大駕于臨晉。

translations.literal: Now plain autumn approaches and the season is fit for campaigning; dukes, marquises, shepherds, guardians, fortress chiefs, and village stalwarts—whether you labor for the state or hold the throne in your hearts—each lead your following and in the first ten days of the tenth month rendezvous with the great host at Linjin.
translations.idiomatic: Autumn's clarity is at hand—the hour to march; nobles, governors, garrison commanders, and local leaders, all who love the dynasty or burn to serve it, bring your commands to Linjin in the opening days of the tenth month to join the imperial army.

sentences.zh: 」於是天水姜延、馮翊寇明、河東王昭、新平張晏、京兆杜敏、扶風馬郎、建忠高平牧官都尉王敏等咸承檄起兵，各有眾數萬，遣使應丕。

translations.literal: " Thereupon Jiang Yan of Tianshui, Kou Ming of Fengyi, Wang Zhao of Hedong, Zhang Yan of Xinping, Du Min of Jingzhao, Ma Lang of Fufeng, Wang Min, commandant of the loyal garrisons of Gaoping, and others all received the summons and raised troops, each with tens of thousands of followers, and sent envoys to answer Fu Pi.
translations.idiomatic: " At once Jiang Yan of Tianshui, Kou Ming of Fengyi, Wang Zhao of Hedong, Zhang Yan of Xinping, Du Min of Jingzhao, Ma Lang of Fufeng, Wang Min of the loyal garrisons at Gaoping, and more took up arms on the strength of the proclamation, fielding armies in the tens of thousands and dispatching messengers to Fu Pi.

sentences.zh: 皆就拜將軍、郡守，封列侯。

translations.literal: All were appointed on the spot generals, administrators, and enfeoffed as marquises of counties.
translations.idiomatic: Each was immediately confirmed as general or prefect and ennobled as a county marquis.

sentences.zh: 冠軍鄧景擁眾五千據彭池，與竇沖為首尾，擊萇平涼太守金熙。

translations.literal: The Champion General Deng Jing, commanding a host of five thousand, held Pengchi and linked with Dou Chong in a pincer, striking Yao Chang's Administrator of Pingliang Jin Xi.
translations.idiomatic: Deng Jing, general of the champions, gathered five thousand men on Pengchi, coordinated with Dou Chong in a two-pronged strike, and hit Jin Xi, Yao Chang's governor of Pingliang.

sentences.zh: 安定北部都尉鮮卑沒奕於率鄯善王胡員吒、護羌中郎將梁苟奴等，與萇左將軍姚方成、鎮遠強京戰于孫丘谷，大敗之。

translations.literal: The Commandant of the Northern Sector of Anding, the Xianbei Moyuyu, leading the King of Shanshan Hu Yuanzha, the General of the Gentlemen of the Household Who Protect the Qiang Liang Gounu, and others, fought Yao Chang's General of the Left Yao Fangcheng and Qiang Jing, general who guards the distance, at Sunqiu Valley and inflicted a great defeat on them.
translations.idiomatic: Moyuyu, Xianbei commandant of northern Anding, marched with Shanshan's king Hu Yuanzha, Liang Gounu of the Qiang guard, and their allies against Yao Fangcheng and Qiang Jing at Sunqiu Valley and shattered the Qiang army.

sentences.zh: 枹罕諸氐以衛平年老，不可以成事業，議廢之，而憚其宗強，連日不決。

translations.literal: The Di clans of Fuhan, because Wei Ping was old and could not accomplish great undertakings, debated deposing him, yet feared the strength of his lineage and for days could not decide.
translations.idiomatic: In Fuhan the Di elders agreed that Wei Ping was too aged to lead, but they hesitated to depose him because his clan was powerful, and the council dragged on without resolution.

sentences.zh: 氐有啖青者，謂諸將曰：「大事宜定，東討姚萇，不可沈吟猶豫。

translations.literal: Among the Di was Dan Qing, who said to the generals: "The great matter ought to be settled; we must march east against Yao Chang—we cannot sink into hesitation.
translations.idiomatic: A Di leader named Dan Qing told the commanders, "We need a decision now: strike east at Yao Chang. Hesitation will undo us.

sentences.zh: 一旦事發，反為人害。

translations.literal: Once the affair breaks out, on the contrary we will be harmed by others.
translations.idiomatic: If we wait until someone else moves first, we will be the ones cut down.

sentences.zh: 諸軍但請衛公會儲眾將，青為諸軍決之。

translations.literal: The various armies need only ask Duke Wei to assemble the gathered generals; Qing will decide it for the armies.
translations.idiomatic: Ask Duke Wei to call a council of every commander—I will settle the question for you.

sentences.zh: 」眾以為然。

translations.literal: " The crowd deemed this right.
translations.idiomatic: " The officers agreed.

sentences.zh: 於是大饗諸將，青抽劍而前曰：「今天下大亂，豺狼塞路，吾曹今日可謂休戚是同，非賢明之主莫可濟艱難也。

translations.literal: Thereupon he feasted the generals greatly; Qing drew his sword and stepped forward, saying: "Now the realm is in great chaos; jackals and wolves block the road—we of this company today may be called to share weal and woe alike; without a worthy and enlightened lord we cannot cross this hardship.
translations.idiomatic: At the banquet Dan Qing stepped forward with naked blade and said, "The empire is chaos; every road is thick with predators. We live or die together—only a capable sovereign can see us through.

sentences.zh: 衛公朽耄，不足以成大事，宜反初服，以避賢路，狄道長苻登雖王室疏屬，而志略雄明，請共立之，以赴大駕。

translations.literal: Duke Wei is decrepit with age and not sufficient to accomplish a great deed; he ought to return to his original garb and yield the path to the worthy. Though Fu Deng, magistrate of Didao, is a distant cadet of the royal house, his aims and stratagems are heroic and clear—I ask that we together establish him and go to join the great host.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Ping is a spent old man—he should step aside for someone fit to rule. Fu Deng of Didao, though only a minor kinsman of the throne, has vision and courage; let us raise him up and march to the emperor's banner.

sentences.zh: 諸君若有不同者，便下異議。

translations.literal: If any among you gentlemen hold a different view, then speak your dissent now.
translations.idiomatic: If anyone disagrees, say so at once.

sentences.zh: 」乃奮劍攘袂，將斬貳己者，眾皆從之，莫敢仰視。

translations.literal: " Thereupon he brandished his sword and rolled up his sleeves, prepared to behead any who would betray him; all followed him and none dared look up.
translations.idiomatic: He waved his sword and bared his arms, ready to kill waverers on the spot; the chiefs submitted and no one met his eye.

sentences.zh: 於是推登為帥，遣使於丕請命。

translations.literal: Thereupon they raised Deng as commander and sent envoys to Fu Pi to request appointment.
translations.idiomatic: They proclaimed Fu Deng their leader and sent messengers to Fu Pi for imperial confirmation.

sentences.zh: 丕以登為征西大將軍、開府儀同三司、南安王、持節及州郡督因其所稱而授之。

translations.literal: Fu Pi made Deng Grand General Who Conquers the West, with privilege of opening a general's office with ceremony equal to the Three Excellencies, Prince of Nan'an, Bearer of the Imperial Insignia, and for provincial and commandery supervision he invested him with whatever titles Deng had claimed.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Pi named him grand general who conquers the west with three-excellency headquarters, prince of Nan'an, tally-bearer, and confirmed whatever regional commands Deng had already taken.

sentences.zh: 又以徐義為右丞相。

translations.literal: He also made Xu Yi Right Chancellor.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Yi became right chancellor.

sentences.zh: 丕留王騰守晉陽，楊輔戍壺關，率眾四萬進據平陽。

translations.literal: Fu Pi left Wang Teng to defend Jinyang, Yang Fu to garrison Huguan, and led forty thousand men forward to occupy Pingyang.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Pi stationed Wang Teng at Jinyang and Yang Fu at Huguan, then moved on Pingyang with forty thousand troops.

sentences.zh: 王統以秦州降姚萇。

translations.literal: Wang Tong surrendered Qinzhou to Yao Chang.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Tong yielded Qinzhou to Yao Chang.

sentences.zh: 慕容永以丕至平陽，恐不自固，乃遣使求假道還東，丕弗許。

translations.literal: Murong Yong, because Fu Pi had reached Pingyang, feared he could not hold his ground, and sent envoys begging a borrowed road to return east; Fu Pi refused.
translations.idiomatic: Murong Yong saw Fu Pi enter Pingyang and feared encirclement; he asked safe passage eastward, but Fu Pi said no.

sentences.zh: 遣王永及苻纂攻之，以俱石子為前鋒都督，與慕容永戰於襄陵。

translations.literal: He dispatched Wang Yong and Fu Zuan to attack him, making Ju Shizi commander of the vanguard, and fought Murong Yong at Xiangling.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Pi sent Wang Yong and Fu Zuan against him with Ju Shizi in the van; the armies met at Xiangling.

sentences.zh: 王永大敗，永及石子皆死之。

translations.literal: Wang Yong was greatly defeated; both Yong and Shizi died in the fighting.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Yong's army was routed; Wang Yong and Ju Shizi both fell.

sentences.zh: 初，苻纂之奔丕也，部下壯士三千餘人，丕猜而忌之。

translations.literal: Earlier, when Fu Zuan had fled to Fu Pi, his following of stalwart warriors numbered more than three thousand, and Fu Pi suspected and envied him.
translations.idiomatic: When Fu Zuan first joined Fu Pi he brought three thousand picked fighters, and Fu Pi regarded him with jealousy and mistrust.

sentences.zh: 及永之敗，懼為纂所殺，率騎數千南奔東垣。

translations.literal: When Yong was defeated, he feared being killed by Zuan and led several thousand cavalry in flight south to Dongyuan.
translations.idiomatic: After Wang Yong's defeat, Fu Pi feared Fu Zuan would kill him and bolted south toward Dongyuan with several thousand horse.

sentences.zh: 晉揚威將軍馮該自陝要擊，敗之，斬丕首，執其太子甯、長樂王壽，送于京師，朝廷赦而不誅，歸之於苻宏。

translations.literal: The Jin general who spreads might, Feng Gai, ambushed him from Shan, defeated him, cut off Fu Pi's head, seized his heir Ning and the Prince of Changle Shou, and sent them to the capital; the court pardoned them and did not execute them, returning them to Fu Hong.
translations.idiomatic: Feng Gai, Jin's general who spreads might, intercepted him at Shan, broke his force, beheaded Fu Pi, and took the crown prince Ning and the prince of Changle, Shou, to the Jin court. Jin spared them and handed them over to Fu Hong.

sentences.zh: 徐義為慕容永所獲，械埋其足，將殺之。

translations.literal: Xu Yi was captured by Murong Yong; they shackled him and buried his feet, intending to kill him.
translations.idiomatic: Murong Yong seized Xu Yi, clamped him in irons with his legs buried in earth, and prepared his execution.

sentences.zh: 義誦《觀世音經》，至夜中，土開械脫，於重禁之中若有人導之者，遂奔楊佺期，佺期以為洛陽令。

translations.literal: Yi chanted the 《Guanshiyin Sutra》; in the middle of the night the earth opened, the fetters came loose, and in the midst of heavy confinement it was as if someone guided him; he fled to Yang Quanqi, who made him magistrate of Luoyang.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Yi recited the 《Guanshiyin Sutra》; at midnight the soil shifted, his bonds fell away, and though he was locked deep in the prison he seemed led by an unseen hand until he reached Yang Quanqi, who appointed him magistrate of Luoyang.

sentences.zh: 苻纂及弟師奴率丕余眾數萬，奔據杏城。

translations.literal: Fu Zuan and his younger brother Shinu led Fu Pi's remaining host of several tens of thousands, fled, and occupied Xingcheng.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Zuan and his brother Shinu gathered Fu Pi's survivors—tens of thousands strong—and withdrew to Xingcheng.

sentences.zh: 苻登稱尊號，偽諡丕為哀平皇帝。

translations.literal: Fu Deng assumed the supreme title and posthumously titled Fu Pi Emperor Aiping of false reign.
translations.idiomatic: When Fu Deng took the throne he gave the late Fu Pi the posthumous title Emperor Aiping.

sentences.zh: 丕之臣佐皆沒慕容永，永乃進據上党之長子，僭稱大號，改元曰中興。

translations.literal: Fu Pi's ministers and aides all fell into Murong Yong's hands; Yong then advanced to occupy Zhangzi in Shangdang, unlawfully assumed the great title, and changed the era name to Zhongxing.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Pi's officials were swallowed up by Murong Yong, who pushed into Zhangzi in Shangdang, declared himself emperor, and adopted the reign name Zhongxing.

sentences.zh: 丕在位二年而敗。

translations.literal: Fu Pi had been on the throne two years when he was defeated.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Pi reigned only two years before his ruin.

sentences.zh: 登字文高，堅之族孫也。

translations.literal: Deng's style name was Wengao; he was a great-grandson of Fu Jian's lineage.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Deng, courtesy Wengao, belonged to a collateral branch of Fu Jian's clan.

sentences.zh: 父敞，健之世為太尉司馬、隴東太守、建節將軍，後為苻生所殺。

translations.literal: His father Chang, in Fu Jian's time, had been marshal to the grand commandant, administrator of Longdong, general who establishes the lineage, and was later killed by Fu Sheng.
translations.idiomatic: His father Fu Chang had served as marshal to the grand commandant, governor of Longdong, and general who establishes the lineage under Fu Jian, until Fu Sheng put him to death.

sentences.zh: 堅即偽位，追贈右將軍、涼州刺史，以登兄同成嗣。

translations.literal: When Fu Jian assumed the false throne, he posthumously awarded Chang the titles General of the Right and Inspector of Liangzhou, and had Deng's elder brother Tongcheng succeed to his line.
translations.idiomatic: After Fu Jian took the throne he posthumously honored Fu Chang as general of the right and inspector of Liangzhou and let Fu Deng's elder brother Tongcheng inherit his line.

sentences.zh: 毛興之鎮上邽，以為長史。

translations.literal: When Mao Xing garrisoned Shanggui, he made him chief clerk.
translations.idiomatic: Mao Xing, holding Shanggui, appointed Fu Deng his chief clerk.

sentences.zh: 登少而雄勇，有壯氣，粗險不修細行，故堅弗之奇也。

translations.literal: From youth Deng was fierce and brave, with a stalwart spirit; he was rough, risky, and did not cultivate petty conduct, therefore Fu Jian did not regard him as remarkable.
translations.idiomatic: Young Fu Deng was bold and truculent, careless of small decorum, so Fu Jian never marked him as exceptional.

sentences.zh: 長而折節謹厚，頗覽書傳。

translations.literal: When grown he bent his will to restraint and became careful and honest, and read fairly widely in texts and commentaries.
translations.idiomatic: In manhood he curbed his temper, grew steady and trustworthy, and read widely among the classics and histories.

sentences.zh: 拜殿上將軍，稍遷羽林監、揚武將軍、長安令，坐事黜為狄道長。

translations.literal: He was appointed General on Palace Duty, gradually promoted to colonel of the feathered forest, General Who Spreads Might, and magistrate of Chang'an; for an offense he was demoted to magistrate of Didao.
translations.idiomatic: He rose from general on palace duty to colonel of the imperial guard, general who spreads might, and magistrate of Chang'an, then lost his post for a fault and became magistrate of Didao.

sentences.zh: 及關中亂，去縣歸毛興。

translations.literal: When Guanzhong fell into chaos, he left the county and returned to Mao Xing.
translations.idiomatic: When Guanzhong collapsed he abandoned his district and rejoined Mao Xing.

sentences.zh: 同成言於興，請以登為司馬，常在營部。

translations.literal: Tongcheng spoke to Xing, asking that Deng be made marshal and constantly kept in the camp staff.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Tongcheng urged Mao Xing to name Fu Deng marshal and keep him always in headquarters.

sentences.zh: 登度量不群，好為奇略，同成常謂之曰：「汝聞不在其位，不謀其政，無數幹時，將為博識者不許。

translations.literal: Deng's capacity and measure were not of the common sort; he loved to devise unusual stratagems. Tongcheng often said to him: "You have heard that he who is not in office does not plan its policies—if without number you meddle in the affairs of the times, men of broad knowledge will not approve.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Deng's mind was not ordinary; he loved bold schemes. Tongcheng warned him, "You know the saying—outside an office you do not shape its policy. Meddle too often and the wise will call you presumptuous.

sentences.zh: 吾非疾汝，恐或不喜人妄豫耳，自是可止。

translations.literal: It is not that I resent you—I only fear others may dislike men who rashly interfere; from here on you may stop.
translations.idiomatic: I do not scorn you, but others hate unsolicited advice. Hold your tongue from now on.

sentences.zh: 汝後得政，自可專意。

translations.literal: If later you obtain power, you may then devote yourself wholly.
translations.idiomatic: When power is yours, you may speak and act as you please.

sentences.zh: 」時人聞同成言，多以為疾登而抑蔽之。

translations.literal: " People who heard Tongcheng's words mostly thought he resented Deng and was suppressing him.
translations.idiomatic: Listeners assumed Tongcheng was jealous and trying to silence Fu Deng.

sentences.zh: 登乃屏跡不妄交遊。

translations.literal: Deng thereupon withdrew from trace and did not recklessly associate or travel.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Deng then kept to himself and avoided casual company.

sentences.zh: 興有事則召之，戲謂之曰：「小司馬可坐評事。

translations.literal: When Xing had business he would summon him, jokingly saying to him: "Little Marshal may sit and judge affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever Mao Xing needed counsel he called him in, teasing, "Let the little marshal hear the case.

sentences.zh: 」登出言輒析理中，興內服焉，然敬憚而不能委任。

translations.literal: " Whenever Deng spoke, his analysis always hit the principle; Xing inwardly admired him, yet respected and feared him and could not delegate full responsibility.
translations.idiomatic: " Fu Deng's judgments were always sound; Mao Xing admired him inwardly yet still distrusted him with real authority.

sentences.zh: 姚萇作亂，遣其弟碩德率眾伐毛興，相持久之。

translations.literal: When Yao Chang rose in rebellion, he sent his younger brother Shuo De to lead a host to attack Mao Xing; they faced each other for a long time.
translations.idiomatic: Yao Chang's revolt sent Yao Shuode against Mao Xing; the two sides glared at each other for months.

sentences.zh: 興將死，告同成曰：「與卿累年共擊逆羌，事終不克，何恨之深！

translations.literal: When Xing was about to die, he told Tongcheng: "With you, sir, I have for years together struck the rebellious Qiang, yet in the end we did not overcome—how deep is the regret!
translations.idiomatic: Dying, Mao Xing said to Tongcheng, "We fought the Qiang rebels together for years and never finished them—my regret is bitter!

sentences.zh: 可以後事付卿小弟司馬，殄碩德者，必此人也。

translations.literal: I may entrust the aftermath to your younger brother the marshal; the one who will destroy Shuo De is surely this man.
translations.idiomatic: Leave the rest to your younger brother, our marshal—he is the man who will finish Shuode.

sentences.zh: 卿可換攝司馬事。」

translations.literal: You, sir, may take over the marshal's duties in his stead."
translations.idiomatic: Take his place as marshal."

sentences.zh: 登既代衛平，遂專統征伐。

translations.literal: Once Deng had replaced Wei Ping, he then held sole command of campaigns.
translations.idiomatic: After Fu Deng succeeded Wei Ping he alone led the armies.

sentences.zh: 是時歲旱眾饑，道殣相望，登每戰殺賊，名為熟食，謂軍人曰：「汝等朝戰，幕便飽肉，何憂於饑！

translations.literal: At this time the year was dry and the masses hungry; corpses littered the roads. Each time Deng killed bandits in battle he called it cooked food, saying to the soldiers: "You fight in the morning, and in the evening you have your fill of meat—why worry about hunger!
translations.idiomatic: Drought and famine left the roads strewn with dead; Fu Deng called enemy corpses "cooked rations" and told his men, "Fight at dawn and you feast on flesh by dusk—what famine need you fear?

sentences.zh: 」士眾從之，啖死人肉，輒飽健能鬥。

translations.literal: " The officers and troops followed him, eating dead men's flesh, and always became sated, strong, and able to fight.
translations.idiomatic: " The army obeyed, fed on the fallen, and grew fierce enough to fight on.

sentences.zh: 姚萇聞之，急召碩德曰：「汝不來，必為苻登所食盡。

translations.literal: When Yao Chang heard of it, he urgently summoned Shuo De, saying: "If you do not come, you will surely be entirely eaten by Fu Deng.
translations.idiomatic: Yao Chang urgently recalled Shuode, warning, "If you delay, Fu Deng will devour you to the last man.

sentences.zh: 」碩德於是下隴奔萇。

translations.literal: " Shuo De thereupon came down from Long and fled to Chang.
translations.idiomatic: " Shuode abandoned the Long uplands and raced to Yao Chang's side.

sentences.zh: 及丕敗，丕尚書寇遺奉丕子渤海王懿、濟北王昶自杏城奔登。

translations.literal: When Fu Pi was defeated, Fu Pi's Director of the Secretariat Kou Yi led Fu Pi's sons the Prince of Bohai Yi and the Prince of Jibei Chang from Xingcheng to flee to Deng.
translations.idiomatic: After Fu Pi's fall, Kou Yi, his director of the secretariat, shepherded the princes Yi of Bohai and Chang of Jibei from Xingcheng to Fu Deng's camp.

sentences.zh: 登乃具丕死問，於是為丕發喪行服，三軍縞素。

translations.literal: Deng then learned fully of Fu Pi's death; thereupon he held mourning for Fu Pi and observed the rites of bereavement; the whole army wore white.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Deng received certain news of Fu Pi's death, proclaimed mourning, and clothed his host in white.

sentences.zh: 登請立懿為主，眾咸曰：「渤海王雖先帝之子，然年在幼沖，未堪多難。

translations.literal: Deng asked to establish Yi as lord; the crowd all said: "Though the Prince of Bohai is a son of the late emperor, his years are yet in tender youth and he cannot bear many hardships.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Deng wished to enthrone Prince Yi, but the officers replied, "The prince of Bohai is the late emperor's son, yet he is a child and cannot bear these trials.

sentences.zh: 國亂而立長君，《春秋》之義也。

translations.literal: When the state is in chaos and one establishes an elder lord—it is the meaning of the 《Spring and Autumn Annals》.
translations.idiomatic: The 《Spring and Autumn Annals》 teach that in times of turmoil the elder heir must rule.

sentences.zh: 三虜跨僭，寇旅殷強，豺狼梟鏡，舉目而是，自厄運之極，莫甚於斯。

translations.literal: The three usurpers stride across the land, their raiding hosts numerous and strong; jackals, owls, and brutes fill every eye—since the nadir of ill fortune, nothing has matched this moment.
translations.idiomatic: Three rebel powers straddle the realm with armies too strong to count; predators seem to throng every hill. Fate has never sunk lower.

sentences.zh: 大王挺劍西州，鳳翔秦、隴，偏師暫接，姚萇奔潰，一戰之功，可謂光格天地。

translations.literal: The Great King drew his sword in the western provinces and soared over Qin and Long; your detached force briefly engaged him and Yao Chang fled in rout—with the merit of one battle you may be said to have outshone heaven and earth.
translations.idiomatic: You raised the west like a dragon over Qin and Long; one clash sent Yao Chang running—a single day's work that dims heaven and earth.

sentences.zh: 宜龍驤武奮，拯拔舊京，以社稷宗廟為先，不可顧曹臧、吳劄一介微節，以失圖運之機，不建中興之業也。

translations.literal: You ought to rouse dragon might and martial fury, rescue and raise the old capital, and put the altars of state and ancestral temple first—you cannot heed the petty scruples of Cao Zang and Wu Zha, miss the moment heaven offers for planning, and fail to build the enterprise of middle restoration.
translations.idiomatic: Rouse your armies, recover the ancient capital, and put the dynasty before private sentiment—do not imitate Cao Zang or Wu Zha's small renunciations and lose heaven's chance to restore the throne.

sentences.zh: 」登於是乙太元十一年僭即皇帝位，大赦境內，改元曰太初。

translations.literal: " Deng thereupon in the eleventh year of Taiyuan unlawfully assumed the imperial dignity, granted a general amnesty within his borders, and changed the era name to Taichu.
translations.idiomatic: " In the eleventh year of Taiyuan Fu Deng declared himself emperor, amnestied his realm, and took the reign name Taichu.

sentences.zh: 立堅神主於軍中，載以輜軿，羽葆青蓋，車建黃旗，武賁之士三百人以衛之，將戰必告，凡欲所為，啟主而後行。

translations.literal: He set up Fu Jian's spirit tablet in the army, carried it in a covered wagon with feathered canopy and green top, the chariot bearing a yellow banner, three hundred picked warriors guarding it; before every battle he was sure to announce it, and in all he wished to do he informed the tablet before acting.
translations.idiomatic: He placed Fu Jian's spirit tablet in a chariot hung with yellow banners, green canopy, and an escort of three hundred guards; before each battle he reported to the late emperor's soul and took no step without that leave.

sentences.zh: 繕甲纂兵，將引師而東，乃告堅神主曰：「維曾孫皇帝臣登，乙太皇帝之靈恭踐寶位。

translations.literal: He repaired armor and gathered weapons, intending to lead the army east, and announced to Fu Jian's spirit tablet: "Thus speaks your great-grandson, the emperor, subject Deng: by the spirit of the Grand Emperor I reverently tread the jeweled throne.
translations.idiomatic: As he readied arms for an eastern march he addressed Fu Jian's tablet: "I, Deng, great-grandson and now emperor, mount the throne in the presence of your spirit.

sentences.zh: 昔五將之難，賊羌肆害於聖躬，實登之罪也。

translations.literal: In the past, at the disaster of the five generals, the bandit Qiang wantonly harmed the sacred person—truly it was Deng's crime.
translations.idiomatic: When the five generals fell and the Qiang struck you down, I failed you—that guilt is mine.

sentences.zh: 今合義旅，眾余五萬，精甲勁兵，足以立功，年谷豐穰，足以資贍。

translations.literal: Now I have united the righteous host; my multitude exceeds fifty thousand; keen armor and stalwart soldiers are sufficient to achieve merit; the year's grain is abundant and sufficient to supply provisions.
translations.idiomatic: Today I lead more than fifty thousand loyal troops, hardened mail and sharp weapons enough to win, and barns full enough to feed them.

sentences.zh: 即日星言電邁，直造賊庭，奮不顧命，隕越為期，庶上報皇帝酷冤，下雪臣子大恥。

translations.literal: This very day, like stars' words and lightning's rush, I go straight to the bandit court, striving without regard for my life, prepared to perish—hoping thereby to answer above for the emperor's bitter wrong and below to wash away the great shame of his servants.
translations.idiomatic: I march this hour like lightning on the rebel court, ready to die if I must, to avenge your murder and cleanse our shame.

sentences.zh: 惟帝之靈，降監厥誠。

translations.literal: May the spirit of the Emperor look down and witness this sincerity.
translations.idiomatic: May your spirit see my heart.

sentences.zh: 」因覷欷流涕。

translations.literal: " Thereupon he sobbed and wept.
translations.idiomatic: He broke down in tears.

sentences.zh: 將士莫不悲慟，皆刻鉾鎧為「死休」字，示以戰死為志。

translations.literal: The generals and soldiers none failed to grieve bitterly; all carved on spears and armor the characters "dead rest," showing that to die in battle was their aim.
translations.idiomatic: Every soldier wept with him and carved the words "dead rest" on helm and mail, vowing to fight to the death.

sentences.zh: 每戰以長槊鉤刃為方圓大陣，知有厚薄，從中分配，故人自為戰，所向無前。

translations.literal: In each battle he used long spears with hooked blades to form great square and round formations, knowing where they were thick and thin and assigning from the center accordingly, so each man fought for himself and none could stand before them.
translations.idiomatic: In battle he drew up squares and circles of long hooked spears, thickening the center or the wings as needed so each man fought as a citadel—none could break his line.

sentences.zh: 初，長安之將敗也，堅中壘將軍徐嵩、屯騎校尉胡空各聚眾五千，據險築堡以自固，而受姚萇官爵。

translations.literal: Earlier, when Chang'an was about to fall, Fu Jian's General of the Central Rampart Xu Song and Colonel of Garrison Cavalry Hu Kong each gathered five thousand men, seized defiles, built forts to secure themselves, and accepted office and noble rank from Yao Chang.
translations.idiomatic: Before Chang'an fell, Xu Song and Hu Kong had each raised five thousand men, walled mountain passes, and taken Yao Chang's commissions.

sentences.zh: 及萇之害堅，嵩等以王禮葬堅於二堡之間。

translations.literal: When Chang harmed Fu Jian, Song and others buried Fu Jian with kingly rites between the two forts.
translations.idiomatic: After Yao Chang murdered Fu Jian they buried him with royal honors between their two strongholds.

sentences.zh: 至是，各率眾降登。

translations.literal: At this point each led his host to surrender to Deng.
translations.idiomatic: Now both brought their followers over to Fu Deng.

sentences.zh: 拜嵩鎮軍將軍、雍州刺史，空輔國將軍、京兆尹。

translations.literal: He appointed Song General Who Guards the Army and Inspector of Yongzhou, Kong General Who Supports the State and Governor of the Capital District.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Deng named Xu Song general who guards the army and inspector of Yongzhou, Hu Kong general who supports the state and governor of Jingzhao.

sentences.zh: 登復改葬堅以天子之禮。

translations.literal: Deng again reburied Fu Jian with the rites due a Son of Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: He reinterred Fu Jian with full imperial ceremony.

sentences.zh: 又僭立其妻毛氏為皇后，弟懿為皇太弟。

translations.literal: He also unlawfully established his wife Lady Mao as empress and his younger brother Yi as imperial younger brother heir.
translations.idiomatic: He named his wife Mao empress and his brother Yi heir apparent.

sentences.zh: 遣使拜苻纂為使持節、侍中、都督中外諸軍事、太師，領大司馬，進封魯王，纂弟師奴為撫軍大將軍、并州牧、朔方公。

translations.literal: He sent envoys to appoint Fu Zuan Bearer of the Imperial Insignia, Palace Attendant, Commander-in-Chief of All Military Affairs Within and Without, Grand Preceptor, concurrently Grand Marshal, advanced to Prince of Lu, and Zuan's younger brother Shinu General Who Pacifies the Army, Governor of Bingzhou, Duke of Shuofang.
translations.idiomatic: Messengers invested Fu Zuan as grand preceptor, commander of all armies, and prince of Lu, with Shinu as general who pacifies the army and governor of Bingzhou, duke of Shuofang.

sentences.zh: 纂怒謂使者曰：「渤海王世祖之孫，先帝之子，南安王何由不立而自尊乎？

translations.literal: Zuan angrily said to the envoy: "The Prince of Bohai is a grandson of Shizu, a son of the late emperor—by what right does the Prince of Nan'an fail to establish him and instead exalt himself?
translations.idiomatic: Fu Zuan raged at the envoy: "The prince of Bohai is Shizu's grandson and the late emperor's son—how dare Nan'an seize the throne himself?

sentences.zh: 」纂長史王旅諫曰：「南安已立，理無中改。

translations.literal: " Zuan's chief clerk Wang Lü remonstrated, saying: "Nan'an is already established; in principle there is no changing it midway.
translations.idiomatic: " His chief clerk Wang Lü urged, "Nan'an already sits the throne; to unseat him now would be folly.

sentences.zh: 賊虜未平，不可宗室之中自為仇敵，原大王遠蹤光武推聖公之義，梟二虜之後，徐更圖之。

translations.literal: The bandit enemies are not yet pacified; you cannot among the imperial clan make yourselves mutual foes—I pray the Great King follow in the tracks of Guangwu's yielding to the Duke of Geng, and after beheading the two bandits, slowly plan further.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels still hold the field—you must not turn kinsman against kinsman. Follow Guangwu's example with the Geng emperor: destroy the two usurpers first, then debate the succession.

sentences.zh: 」纂乃受命。

translations.literal: " Zuan thereupon accepted the command.
translations.idiomatic: " Fu Zuan swallowed his pride and accepted.

sentences.zh: 於是貳縣虜帥彭沛谷、屠各董成、張龍世、新平羌雷惡地等盡應之，有眾十餘萬。

translations.literal: Thereupon the barbarian chiefs of Er County—Peng Peigu, the Tuge Dong Cheng, Zhang Longshi, the Xinping Qiang Lei Edi, and others—all responded to him, having a host of more than one hundred thousand.
translations.idiomatic: Chiefs from Er county—Peng Peigu, the Tuge Dong Cheng, Zhang Longshi, Xinping Qiang Lei Edi—rallied more than a hundred thousand men to his banner.

sentences.zh: 纂遣師奴攻上郡羌酋金大黑、金洛生，大黑等逆戰，大敗之，斬首五千八百。

translations.literal: Zuan sent Shinu to attack the Qiang chiefs of Shang commandery Jin Dahei and Jin Luosheng; Dahei and others met them in battle, were greatly defeated, and five thousand eight hundred heads were cut off.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Zuan sent Shinu against the Qiang lords Jin Dahei and Jin Luosheng of Shang; they gave battle, were routed, and left 5,800 dead.

sentences.zh: 登以竇沖為車騎大將軍、南秦州牧，楊定為大將軍、益州牧，楊璧為司空、梁州牧。

translations.literal: Deng made Dou Chong Grand General of Chariots and Cavalry and Governor of South Qinzhou, Yang Ding Grand General and Governor of Yizhou, Yang Bi Minister of Works and Governor of Liangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Deng named Dou Chong grand general of chariots and cavalry and governor of south Qinzhou, Yang Ding grand general and governor of Yizhou, Yang Bi minister of works and governor of Liangzhou.

sentences.zh: 苻纂敗姚碩德于涇陽，姚萇自陰密距纂，纂退屯敷陸。

translations.literal: Fu Zuan defeated Yao Shuode at Jingyang; Yao Chang himself opposed Zuan from Yinmi; Zuan withdrew and encamped at Fulu.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Zuan beat Yao Shuode at Jingyang until Yao Chang marched from Yinmi; Fu Zuan fell back to Fulu.

sentences.zh: 竇沖攻萇汧、雍二城，克之，斬其將軍姚元平、張略等。

translations.literal: Dou Chong attacked Chang's cities of Qian and Yong, took them, and beheaded his generals Yao Yuanping, Zhang Lüe, and others.
translations.idiomatic: Dou Chong stormed Yao Chang's towns of Qian and Yong, killing generals Yao Yuanping and Zhang Lüe.

sentences.zh: 又與萇戰於汧東，為萇所敗。

translations.literal: He again fought Chang east of Qian and was defeated by Chang.
translations.idiomatic: He fought again east of Qian and lost to Yao Chang.

sentences.zh: 登次於瓦亭。

translations.literal: Deng halted at Wating.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Deng camped at Wating.

sentences.zh: 萇攻彭沛穀堡，陷之，沛穀奔杏城，萇遷陰密。

translations.literal: Chang attacked Peng Peigu's fort, captured it; Peigu fled to Xingcheng; Chang moved to Yinmi.
translations.idiomatic: Yao Chang took Peng Peigu's fortress; Peng fled to Xingcheng while Yao Chang shifted to Yinmi.

sentences.zh: 登征虜、馮翊太守蘭犢率眾二萬自頻陽入于和寧，與苻纂首尾，將圖長安。

translations.literal: Deng's General Who Conquers Barbarians and Administrator of Fengyi Lan Du led twenty thousand men from Pinyang into Hening, linked with Fu Zuan in a pincer, and planned to take Chang'an.
translations.idiomatic: Lan Du, general who conquers barbarians and governor of Fengyi, brought twenty thousand men from Pinyang to Hening to coordinate with Fu Zuan for a strike on Chang'an.

sentences.zh: 師奴勸其兄纂稱尊號，纂不從，乃殺纂，自立為秦公。

translations.literal: Shinu urged his elder brother Zuan to assume the supreme title; Zuan did not follow, whereupon he killed Zuan and unlawfully established himself Duke of Qin.
translations.idiomatic: Shinu pressed Fu Zuan to take the throne; when he refused, Shinu murdered him and styled himself duke of Qin.

sentences.zh: 蘭犢絕之，皆為姚萇所敗。

translations.literal: Lan Du broke with him; both were defeated by Yao Chang.
translations.idiomatic: Lan Du broke contact; both wings were crushed by Yao Chang.

sentences.zh: 登進所胡空堡，戎夏歸之者十有餘萬。

translations.literal: Deng advanced to Hu Kong's fort; those of barbarian and Hua who submitted to him numbered more than one hundred thousand.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Deng pushed into Hu Kong's fortress; over a hundred thousand Chinese and tribesmen rallied to him.

sentences.zh: 姚萇遣其將軍姚方成攻陷徐嵩堡，嵩被殺，悉坑戎士。

translations.literal: Yao Chang sent his general Yao Fangcheng to attack and capture Xu Song's fort; Song was killed, and all the barbarian soldiers were buried alive in pits.
translations.idiomatic: Yao Fangcheng stormed Xu Song's stronghold, slew Xu Song, and buried the garrison alive.

sentences.zh: 登率眾下隴入朝那，姚萇據武都相持，累戰互有勝負。

translations.literal: Deng led his host down from Long into Chaona; Yao Chang held Wudu and they faced each other, fighting repeatedly with mutual victory and defeat.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Deng descended the Long road to Chaona while Yao Chang held Wudu; they skirmished back and forth with shifting fortunes.

sentences.zh: 登軍中大饑，收葚以供兵士。

translations.literal: In Deng's army there was great famine; they gathered mulberries to supply the soldiers.
translations.idiomatic: Famine gripped Fu Deng's camp; he fed his men on wild mulberries.

sentences.zh: 立其子崇為皇太子，弁為南安王，尚為北海王。

translations.literal: He established his son Chong as crown prince, Bian as Prince of Nan'an, and Shang as Prince of Beihai.
translations.idiomatic: He named his sons Chong crown prince, Bian prince of Nan'an, and Shang prince of Beihai.

sentences.zh: 姚萇退還安定。

translations.literal: Yao Chang withdrew to Anding.
translations.idiomatic: Yao Chang pulled back to Anding.

sentences.zh: 登就食新平，留其大軍于胡空堡，率騎萬餘圍萇營，四面大哭，哀聲動人。

translations.literal: Deng went to forage in Xinping, left his great army at Hu Kong's fort, led more than ten thousand cavalry to surround Chang's camp, and on all sides raised great weeping; the sound of grief moved men.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Deng foraged in Xinping, left his main force at Hu Kong's fort, and ringed Yao Chang's camp with ten thousand horsemen, howling grief on every side until the sound shook the enemy.

sentences.zh: 萇惡之，乃命三軍哭以應登，登乃引退。

translations.literal: Chang detested it and ordered the three armies to weep in answer to Deng; Deng thereupon led a withdrawal.
translations.idiomatic: Yao Chang, unnerved, ordered his own army to wail back; Fu Deng then broke off the siege.

sentences.zh: 萇以登頻戰輒勝，謂堅有神驗，亦于軍中立堅神主，請曰：「往年新平之禍，非萇之罪。

translations.literal: Because Deng frequently fought and always won, Chang said that Fu Jian had spiritual verification, and also in the army set up Fu Jian's spirit tablet, praying: "In former years the disaster at Xinping was not Chang's crime.
translations.idiomatic: Since Fu Deng always won, Yao Chang decided Fu Jian's ghost was helping him and set up Fu Jian's tablet in his own camp, pleading, "The Xinping massacre was not my doing.

sentences.zh: 臣兄襄從陝北渡，假路求西，狐死首丘，欲暫見鄉里。

translations.literal: My elder brother Xiang crossed north from the south of Shan, borrowing a road to seek the west; the fox dies with its head toward its mound—he wished briefly to see his homeland.
translations.idiomatic: My brother Xiang crossed from south of Shan bound for the west, like the fox that turns homeward to die—he only wanted to see his native hills once more.

sentences.zh: 陛下與苻眉要路距擊，不遂而沒。

translations.literal: Your Majesty and Fu Mei blocked him on the choke points and struck him; it did not succeed and he perished.
translations.idiomatic: You and Fu Mei tried to cut him off on the vital passes; the attempt failed and he fell.

sentences.zh: 襄敕臣行殺，非臣之罪。

translations.literal: Xiang ordered your subject to carry out the killing—it is not your subject's crime.
translations.idiomatic: Xiang commanded me to strike—that blood is not on my hands alone.

sentences.zh: 苻登陛下末族，尚欲復讎，臣為兄報恥，于情理何負！

translations.literal: Fu Deng, a remote twig of Your Majesty's house, still wishes to take revenge; your subject avenges his elder brother—wherein am I wanting in feeling or principle!
translations.idiomatic: Fu Deng, a distant kinsman of your line, burns to avenge you; I avenge my brother—tell me how that offends heaven or duty!

sentences.zh: 昔陛下假臣龍驤之號，謂臣曰：'朕以龍驤建業，卿其勉之！

translations.literal: In former days Your Majesty lent your subject the title Dragon General and said to your subject: 'I founded the enterprise as Dragon General—do you likewise strive!'
translations.idiomatic: Once you gave me the banner of Dragon General and said, 'I built this realm under that title—now match my zeal!'

sentences.zh: '明詔昭然，言猶在耳。

translations.literal: The bright edict was manifest; the words are still in the ears.
translations.idiomatic: That clear decree still rings in my ears.

sentences.zh: 陛下雖過世為神，豈假手於苻登而圖臣，忘前征時言邪！

translations.literal: Though Your Majesty has passed the world and become a spirit, would you lend your hand to Fu Deng to plot against your subject, forgetting the words of the former expedition!
translations.idiomatic: Now that you are a god, would you truly work through Fu Deng against me and forget what you swore on campaign?

sentences.zh: 今為陛下立神象，可歸休於此，勿計臣過，聽臣至誠。

translations.literal: Now I have set up a spirit image for Your Majesty; you may rest here and be at ease. Do not reckon my faults; heed your subject's utmost sincerity.
translations.idiomatic: I set up this effigy so you may rest; overlook my sins and hear my earnest heart.

sentences.zh: 」登進師攻萇，既而升樓謂萇曰：「自古及今，安有殺君而反立神象請福，望有益乎！

translations.literal: " Fu Deng advanced his army to attack Chang, then mounted a tower and said to Chang: "From antiquity to the present, has there been one who slew his lord, then in turn set up a divine image to beg blessing, and hoped for gain!
translations.idiomatic: Fu Deng pressed his attack, then shouted from a height, "In all history, who ever murdered his king, then raised an idol to beg fortune, and expected it to help?

sentences.zh: 」大呼曰：「殺君賊姚萇出來，吾與汝決之，何為枉害無辜！

translations.literal: " He cried loudly: "The regicide bandit Yao Chang, come out—I will settle it with you! Why do you wrongly harm the guiltless!
translations.idiomatic: "Come out, regicide Yao Chang—face me! Why slaughter the innocent?

sentences.zh: 」萇憚而不應。

translations.literal: " Chang feared him and did not answer.
translations.idiomatic: Yao Chang quailed and gave no reply.

sentences.zh: 萇自立堅神象，戰未有利，軍中每夜驚恐，乃嚴鼓斬象首以送登。

translations.literal: Chang had set up Fu Jian's spirit image himself; the battle brought no advantage, and each night the army was stricken with panic; thereupon with full drumroll he beheaded the image and sent the head to Deng.
translations.idiomatic: Yao Chang's idol of Fu Jian brought only nightly terror; he had the drums beaten, struck off the statue's head, and sent it to Fu Deng.
