sentences.zh: 登將軍竇洛、竇於等謀反發覺，出奔於萇。

translations.literal: Fu Deng's generals Dou Luo and Dou Yu plotted rebellion; the plot was discovered and they fled out to join Chang.
translations.idiomatic: Dou Luo and Dou Yu, Fu Deng's officers, conspired to mutiny; exposed, they defected to Yao Chang.

sentences.zh: 登進討彭池不克，攻彌姐營及繁川諸堡，皆克之。

translations.literal: Fu Deng advanced to attack Pengchi but could not take it; he attacked the Miqi camp and the forts of Fanchuan and captured them all.
translations.idiomatic: He failed at Pengchi but stormed the Miqi camp and every stronghold along Fanchuan.

sentences.zh: 萇連戰屢敗，乃遣其中軍姚崇襲大界，登引師要之，大敗崇于安丘，俘斬二萬五千，進攻萇將吳忠、唐匡於平涼，克之，以尚書苻碩原為前禁將軍、滅羌校尉，戍平涼。

translations.literal: Chang, though repeatedly beaten in successive battles, sent his Central Army Yao Chong to raid Dajie; Deng led his army to intercept him and greatly defeated Chong at Anqiu, capturing and beheading twenty-five thousand; he advanced to attack Chang's generals Wu Zhong and Tang Kuang at Pingliang, took them, and appointed Fu Shuoyuan of the secretariat General of the Forward Guard and Colonel Who Exterminates the Qiang to garrison Pingliang.
translations.idiomatic: Yao Chang kept losing until he sent Yao Chong to strike Dajie; Fu Deng intercepted him at Anqiu, killed or captured twenty-five thousand, then took Pingliang from Wu Zhong and Tang Kuang and left Fu Shuoyuan to hold it.

sentences.zh: 登進據苟頭原以逼安定。

translations.literal: Fu Deng advanced and occupied Goutou Plain to press Anding.
translations.idiomatic: He seized Goutou Plain and tightened the noose on Anding.

sentences.zh: 萇率騎三萬夜襲大界營，陷之，殺登妻毛氏及其子弁、尚，擒名將數十人，驅掠男女五萬餘口而去。

translations.literal: Chang led thirty thousand cavalry in a night raid on the Dajie camp, captured it, killed Deng's wife Lady Mao and his sons Bian and Shang, seized several tens of famous generals, and drove off more than fifty thousand men and women.
translations.idiomatic: Yao Chang struck the Dajie camp by night with thirty thousand horse, slew Fu Deng's empress Mao and princes Bian and Shang, bagged dozens of noted commanders, and carried off fifty thousand captives.

sentences.zh: 登收合餘兵，退據胡空堡，遣使齎書加竇沖大司馬、驃騎將軍、前鋒大都督、都督隴東諸軍事，楊定左丞相、上大將軍、都督中外諸軍事，楊璧大將軍、都督隴右諸軍事。

translations.literal: Deng gathered the remaining troops, withdrew to occupy Hu Kong's fort, sent envoys bearing documents to advance Dou Chong to Grand Marshal, General of Agile Cavalry, Commander-in-Chief of the Vanguard, Supervisor of Military Affairs in Longdong, Yang Ding to Left Chancellor, Supreme Grand General, Commander-in-Chief of All Military Affairs Within and Without, Yang Bi to Grand General, Supervisor of Military Affairs in Longyou.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Deng regrouped at Hu Kong's fort and promoted Dou Chong to grand marshal and Yang Ding to left chancellor with full military authority, Yang Bi to grand general over Longyou.

sentences.zh: 遣沖率見眾為先驅，自繁川趣長安。

translations.literal: He dispatched Chong to lead the troops at hand as vanguard, himself going from Fanchuan toward Chang'an.
translations.idiomatic: Dou Chong led the van toward Chang'an from Fanchuan.

sentences.zh: 登率眾從新平逕據新豐之千戶固。

translations.literal: Deng led the host from Xinping by a direct route to occupy Qianhu Fort of Xinfeng.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Deng cut through Xinping and seized Qianhu fort at Xinfeng.

sentences.zh: 使定率隴上諸軍為其後繼，璧留守仇池。

translations.literal: He ordered Ding to lead the various armies on Longshang as his rear support, while Bi remained to guard Qiuqi.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Ding was to follow with the Long uplands levies; Yang Bi stayed to hold Qiuqi.

sentences.zh: 又命其并州刺史楊政、冀州刺史楊楷率所統大會長安。

translations.literal: He also ordered his Inspector of Bingzhou Yang Zheng and Inspector of Jizhou Yang Kai to lead their commands in a great rendezvous at Chang'an.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Zheng of Bingzhou and Yang Kai of Jizhou were to march on Chang'an for the general muster.

sentences.zh: 萇遣其將軍王破虜略地秦州，楊定及破虜戰于清水之格奴阪，大敗之。

translations.literal: Chang sent his general Wang Polu to seize territory in Qinzhou; Yang Ding and Polu fought at Genu Slope on the Qingshui, and Ding inflicted a great defeat on him.
translations.idiomatic: Yao Chang's Wang Polu raided Qinzhou until Yang Ding shattered him at Genu Ford on the Qingshui.

sentences.zh: 登攻張龍世於鴦泉堡，姚萇救之，登引退。

translations.literal: Deng attacked Zhang Longshi at Yuanquan Fort; Yao Chang came to save him, and Deng led a withdrawal.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Deng besieged Zhang Longshi at Yuanquan until Yao Chang relieved him, forcing Fu Deng to pull back.

sentences.zh: 萇密遣其將任瓫、宗度詐為內應，遣使招登，許開門納之。

translations.literal: Chang secretly sent his generals Ren Chong and Zong Du to pretend to be inner collaborators, dispatched envoys to summon Deng, promising to open the gates and admit him.
translations.idiomatic: Yao Chang secretly ordered Ren Chong and Zong Du to feign treason and invite Fu Deng inside the walls.

sentences.zh: 登以為然。

translations.literal: Deng believed it was so.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Deng believed the ruse.

sentences.zh: 雷惡地馳謂登曰：「姚萇多計略，善御人，必為奸變，願深宜詳思。

translations.literal: Lei Edi rode in haste and said to Deng: "Yao Chang is full of stratagems and skilled at controlling men; he is sure to work a treacherous turn—I pray you think it through most carefully.
translations.idiomatic: Lei Edi galloped up to warn him: "Yao Chang is cunning and knows how to bind men—he will betray you; think twice.

sentences.zh: 」登乃止。

translations.literal: " Deng thereupon stopped.
translations.idiomatic: " Fu Deng called off the attempt.

sentences.zh: 萇聞惡地之詣登也，謂諸將曰：「此羌多奸智，今其詣登，事必無成。

translations.literal: When Chang heard that Edi had gone to Deng, he said to his generals: "This Qiang is full of treacherous cleverness; now that he has gone to Deng, the affair is sure not to succeed.
translations.idiomatic: Yao Chang told his officers, "That Qiang is sly; now that he has warned Fu Deng, the trap is sprung for nothing.

sentences.zh: 」登聞萇懸門以待之，大驚，謂左右曰：「雷征東其殆聖乎！

translations.literal: " Deng heard that Chang had raised the drawbridge to await him, was greatly startled, and said to those at his side: "Lei, General Who Conquers the East, is perhaps a sage!
translations.idiomatic: Learning that Yao Chang had lifted the portcullis in ambush, Fu Deng gasped to his staff, "Lei the east-conquering general must be clairvoyant!

sentences.zh: 微此公，朕幾為豎子所誤。

translations.literal: Without this lord, I would almost have been misled by the stripling.
translations.idiomatic: Without him I would have walked into that boy's snare.

sentences.zh: 」萇攻陷新羅堡。

translations.literal: " Chang attacked and captured Xinluo Fort.
translations.idiomatic: Yao Chang then took Xinluo fort.

sentences.zh: 萇撫風太守齊益男奔登。

translations.literal: Chang's Administrator of Fufeng Qi Yinan fled to Deng.
translations.idiomatic: Qi Yinan, governor of Fufeng under Yao Chang, defected to Fu Deng.

sentences.zh: 登將軍路柴、強武等並以眾降於萇。

translations.literal: Fu Deng's generals Lu Chai, Qiang Wu, and others all led their hosts to surrender to Chang.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Chai, Qiang Wu, and other Fu Deng commanders went over to Yao Chang with their troops.

sentences.zh: 登攻萇將張業生於隴東，萇救之，不克而退。

translations.literal: Deng attacked Chang's general Zhang Yesheng in Longdong; Chang came to his rescue, could not overcome him, and withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Deng struck Zhang Yesheng in Longdong; Yao Chang tried to help but retired without breaking the siege.

sentences.zh: 登將軍魏褐飛攻姚當成於杏城，為萇所殺。

translations.literal: Fu Deng's general Wei Hefei attacked Yao Dangcheng at Xingcheng and was killed by Chang.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Hefei besieged Yao Dangcheng at Xingcheng and died at Yao Chang's hand.

sentences.zh: 馮翊郭質起兵廣鄉以應登，宣檄三輔曰：「義感君子，利動小人。

translations.literal: Guo Zhi of Fengyi raised troops at Guangxiang to answer Deng and proclaimed to the three adjunct capitals: "Righteousness moves gentlemen; profit moves petty men.
translations.idiomatic: Guo Zhi of Fengyi rose at Guangxiang for Fu Deng and told the Guanzhong heartland, "Duty stirs the noble; greed moves the base.

sentences.zh: 吾等生逢先帝堯、舜之化，累世受恩，非常伯納言之子，即卿校牧守之胤，而可坐視豺狼忍害君父！

translations.literal: We have been born to encounter the transformation of Yao and Shun by the late emperor; for generations we have received favor—we are either sons of ministers who remonstrate and speak, or descendants of colonels and shepherds—how can we sit and watch jackals and wolves cruelly harm our lord and father!
translations.idiomatic: We have known nothing but the late emperor's sage rule; our fathers were councilors or governors—shall we sit idle while beasts devour our sovereign?

sentences.zh: 裸屍薦棘，痛結幽泉，山陵無松隧之兆，靈主無清廟之頌，賊臣莫大之甚，自古所未聞。

translations.literal: The naked corpse laid on thorns, grief knotted in the hidden springs; the imperial mound has no sign of pine-lined tunnel, the spirit tablet has no hymn from the pure temple—never has a traitorous minister been greater than this; from antiquity it has not been heard.
translations.idiomatic: His body was stripped and strewn on brambles; no royal tomb receives him, no temple hymn sounds his virtue—such treason is unheard of in any age.

sentences.zh: 雖茹荼之苦，銜蓼之辛，何以諭之！

translations.literal: Though one eat bitter sow-thistle and hold rank smartweed in the mouth—how can that express it!
translations.idiomatic: Bitter herbs and gall cannot describe this pain.

sentences.zh: 姚萇窮凶肆害，毒被人神，於圖讖歷數萬無一分，而敢妄竊重名，厚顏瞬息，日月固所不照，二儀實亦不育。

translations.literal: Yao Chang, utterly vicious, wantonly harms; his poison touches men and spirits; in charts and prophecies and the reckoning of fate he has not one part in ten thousand, yet he dares unlawfully to steal the great name, brazen-faced in a breath; the sun and moon surely do not shine on him, and the two principles in truth do not nurture him.
translations.idiomatic: Yao Chang's cruelty poisons heaven and earth; no omen names him yet he steals the throne—sun and moon should blind him, yin and yang disown him.

sentences.zh: 皇天雖欲絕之，亦將假手於忠節。

translations.literal: Though august heaven may wish to cut him off, it will still lend its hand through loyal integrity.
translations.idiomatic: Heaven may want him dead, but it will use loyal men as its blade.

sentences.zh: 凡百君子，皆夙漸神化，有懷義方，含恥而存，孰若蹈道而沒乎！

translations.literal: All you gentlemen have long been steeped in divine transformation and cherish righteousness in your breasts—to swallow shame and merely survive, how does that compare to treading the right path and perishing!
translations.idiomatic: You have known the emperor's grace—better to die with honor than live shamed.

sentences.zh: 」眾咸然之。

translations.literal: " The crowd all deemed this right.
translations.idiomatic: The listeners agreed.

sentences.zh: 唯鄭縣人苟曜不從，聚眾數千應姚萇。

translations.literal: Only Gou Yao of Zheng County did not follow; he gathered several thousand men and answered Yao Chang.
translations.idiomatic: Only Gou Yao of Zheng rallied thousands for Yao Chang.

sentences.zh: 登以質為平東將軍、馮翊太守。

translations.literal: Deng made Zhi General Who Pacifies the East and Administrator of Fengyi.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Deng named Guo Zhi general who pacifies the east and governor of Fengyi.

sentences.zh: 質遣部將伐曜，大敗而歸。

translations.literal: Zhi sent a subordinate general to attack Yao, was greatly defeated, and returned.
translations.idiomatic: Guo Zhi's lieutenant attacked Gou Yao and limped back beaten.

sentences.zh: 質乃東引楊楷，以為聲援，又與曜戰于鄭東，為曜所敗，遂歸於萇，萇以為將軍。

translations.literal: Zhi thereupon drew Yang Kai eastward as vocal support, again fought Yao east of Zheng, was defeated by Yao, and thereupon returned to Chang, who made him a general.
translations.idiomatic: Guo Zhi then called on Yang Kai, fought Gou Yao east of Zheng, lost, and fled to Yao Chang, who gave him a general's rank.

sentences.zh: 質眾皆潰散。

translations.literal: Zhi's host all scattered and fled.
translations.idiomatic: Guo Zhi's army melted away.

sentences.zh: 登自雍攻萇將金溫于范氏堡，克之，遂渡渭水，攻萇京兆太守韋范于段氏堡，不克，進據曲牢。

translations.literal: Deng from Yong attacked Chang's general Jin Wen at Fan's Fort, took it, thereupon crossed the Wei River, attacked Chang's Administrator of Jingzhao Wei Fan at Duan's Fort, could not take it, advanced and occupied Qulao.
translations.idiomatic: From Yong he stormed Jin Wen at Fan's fort, forded the Wei, failed against Wei Fan at Duan's fort, but seized Qulao.

sentences.zh: 苟曜有眾一萬，據逆方堡，密應登，登去曲牢繁川，次於馬頭願。

translations.literal: Gou Yao had a host of ten thousand, held Nifang Fort, secretly answered Deng; Deng left Qulao and Fanchuan and halted at Mayuanyuan.
translations.idiomatic: Gou Yao held Nifang with ten thousand men in secret league with Fu Deng, who moved from Qulao and Fanchuan to Mayuanyuan.

sentences.zh: 萇率騎來距，大戰敗之，斬其尚書吳忠，進攻新平。

translations.literal: Chang led cavalry to oppose him, fought a great battle and defeated him, beheaded his Director of the Secretariat Wu Zhong, and advanced to attack Xinping.
translations.idiomatic: Yao Chang rode out, routed him, killed Wu Zhong, and marched on Xinping.

sentences.zh: 萇率眾救之，登引退，復攻安定，為萇所敗，據路承堡。

translations.literal: Chang led the host to rescue it; Deng led a withdrawal, again attacked Anding, was defeated by Chang, and occupied Lucheng Fort.
translations.idiomatic: Yao Chang relieved Xinping; Fu Deng struck Anding, lost, and clung to Lucheng fort.

sentences.zh: 是時萇疾病，見苻堅為崇。

translations.literal: At this time Chang was ill and saw Fu Jian as a vengeful ghost.
translations.idiomatic: Yao Chang fell sick and was haunted by Fu Jian's ghost.

sentences.zh: 登聞之，秣馬萬兵，告堅神主曰：「曾孫登自受任執戈，幾將一紀，未嘗不上天錫祐，皇鑒垂矜，所在必克，賊旅冰摧。

translations.literal: When Deng heard of it, he fed ten thousand horses and announced to Fu Jian's spirit tablet: "Great-grandson Deng, from receiving appointment and grasping the spear, is nearly about to complete twelve years; never have I failed to receive heaven's grant of aid and the imperial mirror's downward pity—wherever I have gone I have surely conquered, and the bandit host has shattered like ice.
translations.idiomatic: Hearing this, Fu Deng fattened the horses and told Fu Jian's tablet, "For twelve years I have borne your spear; heaven has blessed every blow and ice has cracked Yao Chang's ranks.

sentences.zh: 今太皇帝之靈降災疢於逆羌，以形類推之，醜虜必將不振。

translations.literal: Now the spirit of the Grand Emperor sends pestilence upon the rebellious Qiang; judging by outward signs, the ugly bandit is sure to weaken.
translations.idiomatic: Your spirit now strikes the Qiang traitor with sickness; the brute must be failing.

sentences.zh: 登當因其隕斃，順行天誅，拯復梓宮，謝罪清廟。

translations.literal: Deng will take advantage of his fall and death, smoothly execute heaven's punishment, rescue and restore the catalpa coffin, and apologize in the pure temple.
translations.idiomatic: I will finish him as he fails, reclaim your coffin, and bow before your shrine.

sentences.zh: 」於是大赦境內，百僚進位二等。

translations.literal: " Thereupon he granted a general amnesty within his borders, and the hundred officials advanced two grades in rank.
translations.idiomatic: He amnestied the realm and raised every official two steps in rank.

sentences.zh: 與萇將姚崇爭麥于清水，累為崇所敗。

translations.literal: He contended with Chang's general Yao Chong for wheat at Qingshui and was repeatedly defeated by Chong.
translations.idiomatic: He sparred with Yao Chong over grain at Qingshui and lost again and again.

sentences.zh: 進逼安定，去城九十餘里。

translations.literal: He advanced to press Anding, ninety-odd li from the city.
translations.idiomatic: He closed to within ninety li of Anding.

sentences.zh: 萇疾小瘳，率眾距登，登去營逆萇，萇遣其將姚熙隆別攻登營，登懼，退還。

translations.literal: Chang's illness slightly improved; he led the host to oppose Deng; Deng left camp to meet Chang; Chang sent his general Yao Xilong separately to attack Deng's camp; Deng feared and withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: Yao Chang rallied from sickness, Fu Deng marched out to meet him, and Yao Xilong's flank attack on the camp forced Fu Deng back.

sentences.zh: 萇夜引軍過登營三十餘里以躡登後。

translations.literal: Chang by night led the army past Deng's camp more than thirty li to tread on Deng's rear.
translations.idiomatic: By night Yao Chang slipped thirty li past Fu Deng's camp to seize his rear.

sentences.zh: 旦而候人告曰：「賊諸營已空，不知所向。

translations.literal: At dawn the scout reported: "The bandits' camps are all empty; we do not know whither they went.
translations.idiomatic: At dawn scouts cried, "The enemy camps are empty—no sign where they went.

sentences.zh: 」登驚曰：「此為何人，去令我不知，來令我不覺，謂其將死，忽然復來，朕與此羌同世，何其厄哉！

translations.literal: " Deng startled said: "What manner of man is this—going makes me not know, coming makes me not aware; I thought he was about to die, then suddenly he returns—I share the age with this Qiang; how bitter is our fate!
translations.idiomatic: "What man is this?" Fu Deng marveled. "He vanishes and appears at will—I thought him dying, yet he returns. To live in one age with that Qiang—what curse is this!

sentences.zh: 」遂罷師還雍。

translations.literal: " Thereupon he dismissed the army and returned to Yong.
translations.idiomatic: He broke camp and withdrew to Yong.

sentences.zh: 以竇沖為右丞相。

translations.literal: He made Dou Chong Right Chancellor.
translations.idiomatic: He named Dou Chong right chancellor.

sentences.zh: 尋而沖叛，自稱秦王，建年號。

translations.literal: Before long Chong rebelled, styling himself Prince of Qin and establishing an era name.
translations.idiomatic: Soon Dou Chong rebelled as king of Qin with his own reign title.

sentences.zh: 登攻之於野人堡，沖請救于姚萇，萇遣其太子興攻胡空堡以救之。

translations.literal: Deng attacked him at Yeren Fort; Chong begged rescue from Yao Chang, and Chang sent his heir apparent Xing to attack Hu Kong's fort to save him.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Deng besieged him at Yeren; Dou Chong begged Yao Chang, who sent crown prince Yao Xing against Hu Kong fort as diversion.

sentences.zh: 登引兵還赴胡空堡，沖遂與萇連和。

translations.literal: Deng led troops back to hurry to Hu Kong's fort; Chong thereupon joined with Chang in alliance.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Deng raced back to Hu Kong, and Dou Chong made peace with Yao Chang.

sentences.zh: 至是萇死，登聞之喜曰：「姚興小兒，吾將折杖以笞之。

translations.literal: At this point Chang died; when Deng heard of it he rejoiced, saying: "Yao Xing the stripling—I will break a rod to flog him.
translations.idiomatic: When Yao Chang died, Fu Deng crowed, "That boy Yao Xing—I will thrash him with a switch.

sentences.zh: 」於是大赦，盡眾而東，攻屠各姚奴、帛蒲二堡，克之，自甘泉向關中。

translations.literal: " Thereupon he granted a general amnesty, led the entire host east, attacked the two forts of the Tuge Yao Nu and Bo Pu, took them, and from Ganquan headed toward Guanzhong.
translations.idiomatic: He amnestied all ranks, marched east, stormed the Tuge forts of Yao Nu and Bo Pu, and drove from Ganquan toward Guanzhong.

sentences.zh: 興追登不及數十里，登從六陌趣廢橋，興將尹緯據橋以待之。

translations.literal: Xing pursued Deng, not reaching him by several tens of li; Deng from Liumo hastened toward the ruined bridge; Xing's general Yin Wei held the bridge awaiting him.
translations.idiomatic: Yao Xing chased him to within a few dozen li; Fu Deng raced for the broken bridge at Liumo where Yin Wei waited.

sentences.zh: 登爭水不得，眾渴死者十二三。

translations.literal: Deng contended for water and could not obtain it; of the host, twelve or thirteen parts died of thirst.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Deng could not win the water; two men in three died of thirst.

sentences.zh: 與緯大戰，為緯所敗，其夜眾潰，登單馬奔雍。

translations.literal: He fought a great battle with Wei and was defeated by Wei; that night the host scattered; Deng on a single horse fled to Yong.
translations.idiomatic: Yin Wei broke him; that night the army dissolved and Fu Deng rode alone to Yong.

sentences.zh: 初，登之東也，留其弟司徒廣守雍，太子崇守胡空堡。

translations.literal: Earlier, when Deng had gone east, he left his younger brother Minister of Education Guang to guard Yong and the crown prince Chong to guard Hu Kong's Fort.
translations.idiomatic: He had left his brother Fu Guang at Yong and crown prince Fu Chong at Hu Kong.

sentences.zh: 廣、崇聞登敗，出奔，眾散。

translations.literal: Guang and Chong, hearing Deng was defeated, went out in flight; the host scattered.
translations.idiomatic: Hearing of his defeat, Fu Guang and Fu Chong fled and their garrisons scattered.

sentences.zh: 登至，無所歸，遂奔平涼，收集遺眾入馬毛山。

translations.literal: When Deng arrived, he had nowhere to return; thereupon he fled to Pingliang, gathered the scattered host, and entered Maomao Mountain.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Deng found no refuge at Yong, bolted to Pingliang, scraped together stragglers, and climbed Maomao Mountain.

sentences.zh: 興率眾攻之，登遣子汝陰王宗質於隴西鮮卑乞伏乾歸，結婚請援，乾歸遣騎二萬救登。

translations.literal: Xing led the host to attack him; Deng sent his son the Prince of Ruyin Zong as hostage to the Longxi Xianbei Qifu Gangui, allied by marriage and begged aid; Gangui sent twenty thousand cavalry to rescue Deng.
translations.idiomatic: Yao Xing closed in; Fu Deng sent prince Zong of Ruyin as hostage to Qifu Gangui of Longxi Xianbei, sealed the tie with a marriage, and won twenty thousand horsemen.

sentences.zh: 登引軍出迎，與興戰于山南，為興所敗，登被殺。

translations.literal: Deng led the army out to meet them and fought Xing south of the mountain; he was defeated by Xing and Deng was killed.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Deng marched out to join them but Yao Xing cut him down south of the range.

sentences.zh: 在位九年，時年五十二。

translations.literal: He had been on the throne nine years; at the time of death his years were fifty-two.
translations.idiomatic: He had reigned nine years and died at fifty-two.

sentences.zh: 崇奔於湟中，僭稱尊號，改元延初。

translations.literal: Chong fled to Huangzhong, unlawfully assumed the supreme title, and changed the era name to Yanchu.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Chong fled to Huangzhong, declared himself emperor, and took the reign name Yanchu.

sentences.zh: 偽諡登曰高皇帝，廟號太宗。

translations.literal: They posthumously titled Deng Emperor Gao with temple name Taizong.
translations.idiomatic: They gave Fu Deng the temple name Taizong and posthumous title Emperor Gao.

sentences.zh: 崇為乾歸所逐，崇、定皆死。

translations.literal: Chong was driven by Gangui; both Chong and Ding died.
translations.idiomatic: Qifu Gangui drove out Fu Chong; both Fu Chong and Yang Ding perished.

sentences.zh: 始，健以穆帝永和七年僭立，至登五世，凡四十有四歲，以孝武帝太元十九年滅。

translations.literal: In the beginning, Fu Jian the dynastic founder in the seventh year of Yonghe of Emperor Mu unlawfully established himself; down to Deng it was five generations, altogether forty-four years, and in the nineteenth year of Taiyuan of Emperor Xiaowu they were destroyed.
translations.idiomatic: From Fu Jian the founder's coup in Yonghe 7 (Emperor Mu of Jin) through five generations to Fu Deng, the state lasted forty-four years until it perished in Taiyuan 19 under Emperor Xiaowu.

sentences.zh: 索泮，字德林，敦煌人也。

translations.literal: Suo Pan, style name Delin, was a man of Dunhuang.
translations.idiomatic: Suo Pan, courtesy Delin, came from Dunhuang.

sentences.zh: 世為冠族。

translations.literal: For generations they were a capped-gentry clan.
translations.idiomatic: His family ranked among the great houses for generations.

sentences.zh: 泮少時遊俠，及長，變節好學，有佐世才器。

translations.literal: In youth Pan was a wandering knight; when grown he changed his ways, loved learning, and had talent and capacity to aid the age.
translations.idiomatic: Young Suo Pan lived by the sword; grown, he turned scholar and showed statesman's gifts.

sentences.zh: 張天錫輔政，以泮為冠軍、記室參軍。

translations.literal: When Zhang Tianxi assisted in government, he made Pan Champion General and secretary in the headquarters.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Tianxi, as regent, named him champion general and headquarters secretary.

sentences.zh: 天錫即位，拜司兵，歷位禁中錄事。

translations.literal: When Tianxi assumed the throne, he appointed him Director of Soldiers, and he successively held the post of recorder of affairs within the palace.
translations.idiomatic: When Tianxi took the throne, Suo Pan became director of the bureau of soldiers and palace recorder.

sentences.zh: 執法禦掾，州府肅然，郡縣改跡。

translations.literal: He enforced the law as supervising clerk; the provincial headquarters were sternly ordered, commanderies and counties changed their tracks.
translations.idiomatic: As supervising clerk he enforced the code until yamen and countryside mended their ways.

sentences.zh: 遷羽林左監，有勤幹之稱。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Colonel of the Feathered Forest Left and had a reputation for diligent capability.
translations.idiomatic: Promoted to colonel of the left imperial guard, he was known for tireless competence.

sentences.zh: 出為中壘將軍、西郡武威太守、典戎校尉。

translations.literal: He went out as General of the Central Rampart, Administrator of Xijun and Wuwei, and Colonel in Charge of the Tribes.
translations.idiomatic: He left court as general of the central rampart, governor of Xijun and Wuwei, and colonel of the tribes.

sentences.zh: 政務寬和，戎夏懷其惠，天錫甚敬之。

translations.literal: His government affairs were lenient and harmonious; barbarian and Chinese cherished his kindness, and Tianxi greatly respected him.
translations.idiomatic: His rule was mild; tribesmen and Chinese alike loved him, and Zhang Tianxi honored him deeply.

sentences.zh: 苻堅見而歎曰：「涼州信多君子！

translations.literal: Fu Jian saw him and sighed, saying: "Liangzhou truly has many gentlemen!
translations.idiomatic: Fu Jian met him and exclaimed, "Liangzhou breeds true gentlemen!

sentences.zh: 」既而以泮河西德望，拜別駕。

translations.literal: " Thereupon, because of Pan's virtue and standing west of the River, he appointed him aide-de-camp.
translations.idiomatic: "He then made Suo Pan provincial aide for his reputation west of the Yellow River.

sentences.zh: 呂光既克姑臧，泮固郡不降，光攻而獲之。

translations.literal: After Lü Guang had taken Guzang, Pan held his commandery firm and would not surrender; Guang attacked and captured him.
translations.idiomatic: When Lü Guang seized Guzang, Suo Pan held his ground until Lü Guang stormed him out.

sentences.zh: 光曰：「孤既平西域，將赴難京師，梁熙無狀，絕孤歸路，此朝延之罪人，卿何意阻郡固迷，自同元惡！

translations.literal: Guang said: "I have already pacified the Western Regions and was about to hurry to the capital's distress; Liang Xi behaved disgracefully, cutting off my road home—he is this court's criminal—what intention had you to block the commandery, stubbornly lost, and make yourself the same as the arch-villain!
translations.idiomatic: Lü Guang said, "I conquered the west to save the throne; Liang Xi blocked my road—that traitor to the court—why did you bar your gates like him?

sentences.zh: 」泮厲色責光曰：「將軍受詔討叛胡，可受詔亂涼州邪？

translations.literal: " Pan with stern countenance rebuked Guang, saying: "The general received an edict to punish the rebellious Hu—may one receive an edict to throw Liangzhou into chaos?
translations.idiomatic: "Suo Pan answered coldly, "You were ordered to crush rebel Hu, not to ravage Liangzhou.

sentences.zh: 寡君何罪，而將軍害之？

translations.literal: What crime had our lord, yet the general harmed him?
translations.idiomatic: What crime had our prince that you destroyed him?

sentences.zh: 泮但苦力寡，不能固守以報君父之讎，豈如逆氐彭濟望風反叛！

translations.literal: Pan only bitterly lacked strength, could not hold firm to avenge lord and father's enmity—how could he be like the rebellious Di Peng Ji, who at the wind's rumor rebelled!
translations.idiomatic: I failed only from weakness—I could not hold the walls to avenge my prince. Would I resemble Peng Ji the Di, who turned coat at the first rumor?

sentences.zh: 主滅臣死，禮之常也。

translations.literal: When the lord perishes the minister dies—this is the constant of ritual.
translations.idiomatic: When the sovereign falls, the loyal servant follows him—that is the rite.

sentences.zh: 」乃就刑於市，神色不變。

translations.literal: " Thereupon he went to execution in the marketplace, his expression unchanged.
translations.idiomatic: He walked to the market block without flinching.

sentences.zh: 弟菱，有俊才，仕張天錫為執法中郎、冗從右監。

translations.literal: His younger brother Ling had outstanding talent; he served Zhang Tianxi as Director of Law Enforcement of the Gentlemen of the Household and Supervisor of the Right of the Redundant Retinue.
translations.idiomatic: His brother Suo Ling, a brilliant man, served Zhang Tianxi as director of law enforcement and right supervisor of the supernumerary guard.

sentences.zh: 苻堅世至伏波將軍、典農都尉，與泮俱被害。

translations.literal: In Fu Jian's age he reached General Who Crosses the Waves and Chief Commandant of Agriculture; together with Pan he was murdered.
translations.idiomatic: Under Fu Jian he rose to general who crosses the waves and chief commandant of agriculture and died with Suo Pan.

sentences.zh: 徐嵩，字元高，盛之子也。

translations.literal: Xu Song, style name Yuangao, was the son of Sheng.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Song, courtesy Yuangao, was Xu Sheng's son.

sentences.zh: 少以清白著稱。

translations.literal: From youth he was famed for purity and integrity.
translations.idiomatic: Even young he was known for spotless honor.

sentences.zh: 苻堅時舉賢良，為郎中，稍遷長安令，貴戚子弟犯法者，嵩一皆考竟，請托路絕。

translations.literal: In Fu Jian's time he was recommended as worthy and good, became a gentleman consultant, gradually was promoted to magistrate of Chang'an; as for noble relatives' sons who violated the law, Song investigated them all to the end, and the path of private pleading was cut off.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Jian's court drafted him as an outstanding talent; he rose to magistrate of Chang'an and prosecuted every princeling who broke the law until no one could buy mercy.

sentences.zh: 堅甚奇之，謂其叔父成曰：「人為長吏，故當應耳。

translations.literal: Fu Jian greatly marveled at him, saying to his uncle Cheng: "Men who become senior magistrates generally muddle through.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Jian told his uncle Cheng, "Most county chiefs just muddle through.

sentences.zh: 此年少落落，有端貳之才。

translations.literal: This youth stands apart; he has the capacity of a chief minister.
translations.idiomatic: This boy holds himself apart—he has the makings of a pillar of state.

sentences.zh: 」遷守始平郡，甚有威惠。

translations.literal: " He was transferred to defend Shiping commandery, and had great awe-inspiring kindness.
translations.idiomatic: He was posted to Shiping, where he ruled with equal awe and mercy.

sentences.zh: 及壘陷，姚方成執而數之，嵩厲色謂方成曰：「汝姚萇罪應萬死，主上止黃眉之斬而宥之，叨據內外，位為列將，無犬馬識養之誠，首為大逆。

translations.literal: When the rampart fell, Yao Fangcheng seized him and rebuked him; Song with stern countenance said to Fangcheng: "Your Yao Chang's crimes deserved ten thousand deaths; the Sovereign stayed the execution at Huangmei and spared him; he presumptuously occupied inner and outer posts, ranked as a column general, yet had no sincerity of dog-and-horse nurture, and was first in the great treason.
translations.idiomatic: When the fort fell, Yao Fangcheng taunted him; Xu Song answered, "Yao Chang deserved death a thousand times; the emperor spared him after Huangmei, yet he climbed to high command without a dog's loyalty and led the treason himself.

sentences.zh: 汝曹羌輩豈可以人理期也！

translations.literal: How can you lot of Qiang be expected to follow human reason!
translations.idiomatic: You Qiang cannot be reasoned with as men!

sentences.zh: 何不速殺我，早見先帝，取姚萇於地下。

translations.literal: Why not kill me quickly, that I may soon see the late emperor and seize Yao Chang in the underworld.
translations.idiomatic: Kill me now so I may join the late emperor and drag Yao Chang down to hell.

sentences.zh: 」方成怒，三斬嵩，漆其首為便器。

translations.literal: " Fangcheng in anger hacked Song three times, lacquered his head, and made it a urinal.
translations.idiomatic: Yao Fangcheng butchered him, lacquered his skull, and turned it into a chamber pot.

sentences.zh: 登哭之哀慟，贈車騎大將軍、儀同三司，諡曰忠武。

translations.literal: Deng wept for him with bitter grief, posthumously awarding Grand General of Chariots and Cavalry with ceremony equal to the Three Excellencies, posthumous title Loyal and Martial.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Deng mourned him bitterly and posthumously named him grand general of chariots and cavalry with three-excellency honors, styled Loyal and Martial.

sentences.zh: 史臣曰：自兩京殄覆，九土分崩，赤縣成蛇豕之墟，紫宸遷蛙黽之穴，干戈日用，戰爭方興，猶逐鹿之並驅，若瞻烏之靡定。

translations.literal: The historians say: From the two capitals' destruction and the nine provinces' collapse, the Red Lands became lairs of serpents and swine, the Purple Palace moved to the burrow of frogs—spears and halberds daily employed, war just rising—like deer chased together, like crows on the roof with nowhere settled.
translations.idiomatic: The chroniclers write: When both capitals fell and the realm shattered, the heartland turned to beasts' dens and the throne to a swamp court—arms never rested, rivals raced like hunters after deer, fate hung like roosting crows.

sentences.zh: 苻洪擅蠻陬之桀黠，乘羯虜之危亡，乃附款江東而志圖關右，禍生蠆毒，未逞狼心。

translations.literal: Fu Hong monopolized the craftiness of the southern barbarian marches, exploited the peril and doom of the Jie captives, then pledged allegiance east of the Yangzi while intending to map Guanxi—disaster hatched from scorpion venom, the wolfish heart not yet displayed.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Hong used frontier cunning while the Jie crumbled, bowed to the south while eyeing the northwest—poison already in the sting before the wolf showed his teeth.

sentences.zh: 健既承家，克隆凶緒，率思歸之眾，投山西之隙，據億丈之岩險，總三秦之果銳，敢窺大寶，遂竊鴻名，校數奸雄，有可言矣。

translations.literal: Jian, having inherited the house, further enlarged the evil thread, led the host that longed to return, cast himself into the breach west of the mountains, held fast to cliffs ten thousand fathoms high, commanded the keen edge of the three Qins, dared to peer at the great treasure, thereupon stole the grand name—measured against the reckoning of crafty heroes, there is something to be said.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Jian the heir widened that dark legacy, marched homesick veterans through the mountain gap, seized the sheer heights of the three Qin, dared covet the throne, and stole a king's title—among scheming strongmen he counts for something.

sentences.zh: 長生慘虐，稟自率由。

translations.literal: Changsheng was cruel and violent, born from following his own bent.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Sheng's savagery flowed from indulging every impulse.

sentences.zh: 睹辰象之災，謂法星之夜飲；

translations.literal: Seeing disaster in the astral signs, he called it the law star drinking by night;
translations.idiomatic: He read doom in the stars and called it the planet of law drinking by night;

sentences.zh: 忍生靈之命，疑猛獸之朝饑。

translations.literal: Sparing the lives of the people, he suspected the morning hunger of fierce beasts.
translations.idiomatic: He spared the people yet suspected them like hungry beasts at dawn.

sentences.zh: 但肆毒于刑殘，曾無心於戒懼。

translations.literal: He only wantoned poison in mutilating punishments, never once had a mind for caution and fear.
translations.idiomatic: He reveled in torture and never knew fear.

sentences.zh: 招亂速禍，不亦宜乎！

translations.literal: Calling chaos and hastening calamity—was it not fitting!
translations.idiomatic: Small wonder he summoned rebellion and ruin.

sentences.zh: 永固雅量瑰姿，變夷眾夏，葉魚龍之謠詠，挺草付之休征，克翦奸回，纂承偽曆，遵明王之德教，闡先聖之儒風，撫育黎元，憂勤庶政。

translations.literal: Yonggu had capacious measure and splendid bearing, transformed barbarians and gathered the Hua, harmonized the fish-and-dragon songs and chants, displayed the propitious omen of 'grass' and 'fu,' cut down treacherous evil, inherited the false calendar, followed the enlightened king's virtuous instruction, opened the former sages' Confucian wind, nurtured the black-haired people, and toiled anxiously at the myriad policies.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Jian, styled Yonggu, had the bearing of a founder: he won over tribes and Chinese alike, fulfilled the prophecy of the Fu surname, purged traitors, took the illicit throne, promoted Confucian teaching, and labored for his people.

sentences.zh: 王猛以宏材緯軍國，苻融以懿戚贊經綸，權薛以諒直進規謨，鄧、張以忠勇恢威略，俊賢效足，杞梓呈才，文武兼施，德刑具舉。

translations.literal: Wang Meng with grand talent wove army and state; Fu Rong with noble kinship aided the great weave; Quan and Xue with honest straightness advanced counsel and plans; Deng and Zhang with loyalty and courage enlarged might and strategy—outstanding worthies lent their feet, catalpa and ziziphus displayed their talents; civil and military were both deployed, virtue and punishment alike raised.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Meng ran state and army; Fu Rong, kinsman, shared the planning; Quan Yi and Xue Zan spoke plain truth; Deng Qiang and Zhang Ci showed loyal valor—fine timber filled every office, both culture and law were served.

sentences.zh: 乃平燕定蜀，擒代吞涼，跨三分之二，居九州之七，遐荒慕義，幽險宅心，因止馬而獻歌，托棲鸞以成頌，因以功侔曩烈，豈直化洽當年！

translations.literal: Thereupon they pacified Yan, settled Shu, captured Dai, swallowed Liang, straddled two of three parts, occupied seven of nine provinces; the distant wilds admired righteousness, the hidden defiles took heart; they halted horses and presented songs, lodged phoenixes and completed hymns—thereby their merit matched ancient exemplars; how could it be only transforming harmony in their own age!
translations.idiomatic: They crushed Yan, took Shu, seized Dai, absorbed Liang, held two-thirds of the realm and seven-ninths of the nine domains; distant lands offered allegiance, odes hailed the conqueror—merit to rival the ancients, not merely a passing peace.

sentences.zh: 雖五胡之盛，莫之比也。

translations.literal: Though the Five Hu flourished, none could compare with them.
translations.idiomatic: Even at the height of the Five Hu, none matched their power.

sentences.zh: 既而足己誇世，愎諫違謀，輕敵怒鄰，窮兵黷武。

translations.literal: Then, content with himself and boasting to the world, stubborn against remonstrance and contrary to counsel, he slighted enemies and enraged neighbors, exhausted the army and abused arms.
translations.idiomatic: Then he grew smug, spurned advice, provoked neighbors, and exhausted his armies.

sentences.zh: 懟三正之未葉，恥五運之猶乖，傾率土之師，起滔天之寇，負其犬羊之力，肆其吞噬之能。

translations.literal: Resenting that the three beginnings had not yet aligned, shamed that the five revolutions were still awry, he tilted the armies of the whole realm, raised bandits that touched heaven, relied on brute strength of dog and sheep, and wantoned his power to swallow all.
translations.idiomatic: Fuming that heaven's cycle had not crowned him, he mobilized every soldier, raised a host that blotted the sky, and trusted barbarian might to devour all.

sentences.zh: 自謂戰必勝，攻必取，便欲鳴鸞禹穴，駐蹕疑山，疏爵以侯楚材，築館以須歸命。

translations.literal: He deemed himself sure to win every battle and take every city, and wished to halt his phoenix carriage at Yu's cavern, plant his halberd-screen at Mount Yi, enfeoff marquises among Chu talent, build lodges to await those who would surrender.
translations.idiomatic: He believed every blow would land, dreamed of halting at Yu's grotto and Mount Yi, ennobling Jin gentry and waiting for surrender in guest halls.

sentences.zh: 曾弗知人道助順，神理害盈，雖矜涿野之強，終致昆陽之敗。

translations.literal: He never knew that the human way aids the obedient and the divine pattern harms the proud—though he boasted of Zhuolu's might, in the end he met Kunyang's defeat.
translations.idiomatic: He did not see that heaven favors the just and punishes pride—boasting like the tyrant of Zhuolu, he reenacted Kunyang's rout.

sentences.zh: 遂使凶渠候隙，狡寇伺間，步搖啟其禍先，燒當乘其亂極，宗社遷於他族，身首罄於賊臣，貽戒將來，取笑天下，豈不哀哉！

translations.literal: Thereupon he caused the vicious chieftain to watch for a crack, the cunning bandit to spy for an opening—Buyao opened the disaster's first step, Shaodang rode their extremity of chaos; the altars of state moved to another clan, body and head were spent on traitorous ministers—leaving a warning to later ages, inviting laughter under heaven—was it not pitiful!
translations.idiomatic: So the jackals waited their chance: Murong Buyao struck first, Shaodang Qiang seized the chaos; the dynasty passed to aliens, Fu Jian's corpse fell to traitors—a lesson and a mockery for the world.

sentences.zh: 豈不謬哉！

translations.literal: Was it not erroneous!
translations.idiomatic: What folly!

sentences.zh: 苻丕承亂僭竊，尋及傾敗，斯可謂天之所廢，人不能支。

translations.literal: Fu Pi inherited chaos and stole the throne, soon met overturn and defeat—this may be called what heaven casts off, which man cannot sustain.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Pi seized the throne amid ruin and quickly fell—heaven had withdrawn its mandate; no man could prop him up.

sentences.zh: 苻登集離散之兵，厲死休之志，雖眾寡不敵，難以立功，而義烈慷慨，有足稱矣。

translations.literal: Fu Deng gathered scattered troops and sharpened the will to 'dead rest'; though many and few did not match and it was hard to achieve merit, yet in righteous ardor and generous spirit there was something to praise.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Deng rallied broken armies and the vow to fight to the death; outnumbered, he won little ground, yet his fervor deserves remembrance.

sentences.zh: 贊曰：洪惟壯勇，威棱氐種。

translations.literal: The encomium says: Hong was stalwart and brave; his terror struck the Di tribes.
translations.idiomatic: The ode sings: Fu Hong, bold and fierce, awed the Di.

sentences.zh: 健藉世資，遂雄關、隴。

translations.literal: Jian relied on inherited capital, thereupon dominated the pass and Long.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Jian rode his father's power to master the pass and Long.

sentences.zh: 長生昏虐，敗不旋踵。

translations.literal: Changsheng was benighted and cruel; defeat came before the heel could turn.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Sheng's blind cruelty brought ruin overnight.

sentences.zh: 永固禎祥，肇自龍驤。

translations.literal: Yonggu's auspicious signs began from Dragon General.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Jian's fortune rose when he took the title Dragon General.

sentences.zh: 垂旒負扆，竊帝圖王。

translations.literal: Jade pendants hanging, he backed the screen—he stole the emperor's plan and the king's map.
translations.idiomatic: He donned the crown, faced the court—yet his throne was theft.

sentences.zh: 患生縱敵，難起矜強。

translations.literal: Disaster arose from sparing the foe; peril grew from boasting of strength.
translations.idiomatic: Mercy to enemies bred calamity; pride in arms invited doom.

sentences.zh: 丕、登僭假，淪胥以亡。

translations.literal: Fu Pi and Fu Deng presumptuously borrowed the throne and sank together into extinction.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Pi and Fu Deng clung to a stolen title and perished together.
